ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r1.claim: The discussion identifies divining arrows and related practices, including augury by birds or beasts and taking omens from books, some still practiced today.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r1.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل الزجر بالطير وبالوحش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r2.claim: The verse stacks several emphases: إنما, associating wine and gambling with idols if الأنصاب means idols, calling them filth, attributing them to Satan, commanding avoidance, and promising success for avoiding them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r2.anchor: وقد اجتمعت أنواع من التأكيد في الآية منها التصدير بإنما وقران الخمر والميسر بالأصنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r3.claim: A hadith compares the habitual wine drinker to an idol worshipper.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r4.claim: Wine comes first because the occasion of revelation involved its harmful effects and because it encompasses sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r4.anchor: وبدئ بالخمر لأن سبب النزول إنما وقع بها من الفساد ولأنها جماع الإثم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r5.claim: At the time of revelation, Medina's wine was mostly made from honey, dates, raisins, wheat, and barley, with little made from grapes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r5.anchor: وكانت خمر المدينة حين نزولها الغالب عليها كونها من العسل ومن التمر ومن الزبيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r6.claim: Muslims unanimously forbid both small and large amounts of pure grape wine, whether heated or mixed with nothing; most also forbid a small amount of any drink whose large amount intoxicates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r6.anchor: وقد أجمع المسلمون على تحريم القليل والكثير من خمر العنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r7.claim: Jurists differ over non-grape drinks that do not intoxicate in small amounts but do in large amounts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r7.anchor: والخلاف فيما لا يسكر قليله ويسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب مذكور في كتب الفقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that some infer all filth is forbidden because carrion, blood, and pork are also called filth; he regards that inference as problematic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد خرج قوم تحريم الخمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r9.claim: Avoidance means putting something to the side or at a distance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r9.anchor: والاجتناب أن تجعل الشيء جانبا وناحية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r10.claim: Calling these acts Satan's work is figurative exaggeration that magnifies their ugliness; the author compares it with Moses striking a man and the deed being called Satan's work.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r10.anchor: جعلت من عمله وفعله ونسبت إليه على جهة المجاز والمبالغة في كمال تقبيحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r11.claim: The pronoun in فاجتنبوه refers to the stated filth and therefore commands avoidance of all four listed things themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r11.anchor: والضمير في فاجتنبوه عائد على الرجس المخبر عنه من الأربعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead refers the pronoun to an omitted noun, such as the conduct or consumption of wine and gambling.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r13.claim: There is no need to posit an omitted noun: directly calling the four things filth is more forceful, as when the Qur'an calls polytheists impure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p357/r13.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تقدير هذا المضاف بل الحكم على هذه الأربعة أنفسها أنها رجس أبلغ

DURR-FULL:v7p501/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r2.claim: The Prophet warns that the persistent wine drinker, the disobedient, and the person who reminds others of a gift will not enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يدخل الجنة مدمن الخمر ولا العاق ولا المنان

DURR-FULL:v7p501/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers were troubled by the warning, then identifies the disobedient through this verse, the one who reminds through 2:264, and the wine drinker through 5:90.
DURR-FULL:v7p501/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يدخل الجنة مدمن الخمر ولا العاق ولا المنان قال ابن عباس

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r20.claim: Its rulings address wine and gambling in 5:90–91.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r35.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r35.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r35.claim: Satan makes false promises and incites hostility between people, sometimes through wine and gambling.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r35.anchor: making them (false) promises (4:120; 14:22; 17:64); inciting evil between them (12:100; 17:53)

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r6.claim: Khamr is the familiar intoxicant, named for covering or clouding the intellect.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r6.anchor: فالخمر معروف وهو ما خامر العقل، وقد فسرناه

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r7.claim: Maysir means gambling generally; its original form was wagering on a slaughtered camel, with shares drawn by lots.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r7.anchor:
والميسر القمار
كله، وأصله إنه كان قمارا في الجزور، وكانوا يقسمون الجزور

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r8.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the camel was divided into twenty-eight shares.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r8.anchor:
في قول
الأصمعي على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r9.claim: Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani says the camel was divided into ten shares.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r9.anchor:
وفي قول أبي عمرو الشيباني على عشرة
أجزاء

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r10.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says he does not know how many shares the camel was divided into.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة لا أعرف عدد الأجزاء

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r11.claim: People used wooden arrows with names to draw shares, and a winner received a portion according to his draw; all gambling falls under maysir.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r11.anchor: وكانوا يضربون عليها بالقداح وهي سهام خشب. لها أسماء

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r12.claim: Wine, gambling, divining by arrows, and idol worship are condemned as rijs, an umbrella term for abhorrent acts that Satan entices.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r12.anchor:
فأعلم الله أن القمار والخمر والاستقسام بالأزلام وعبادة الأوثان رجس.
والرجس في اللغة اسم لكل ما استقذر من عمل

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r13.claim: The verbs رجس الرجل يرجس and رجس يرجس describe doing an ugly deed.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r13.anchor: يقال رجس الرجل يرجس، ورجس يرجس، إذا عمل عملا قبيحا

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r14.claim: Rijs with an open rāʾ means a loud sound; the word also evokes an ugly deed whose mention rises in abhorrence, and a رجاس cloud or thunder is loud.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r14.anchor:
والرجس بفتح الراء
شدة الصوت، فكان الرجس العمل الذي يقبح ذكره، ويرتفع في القبح.
ويقال سحاب ورعد رجاس إذا كان شديد الصوت

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r15.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r15.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r15.claim: The poet's word رجاس is cited as evidence for the sense of loud sound.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r15.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وكل رجاس يسوق الرجسا

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r16.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r16.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r16.claim: The word الرجز with zāy means punishment or an act that leads to punishment; the cited occurrence means punishment, while another is interpreted as idol worship.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r16.anchor:
وأما الرجز بالزاي فالعذاب، أو العمل الذي يؤدي إلى العذاب.
قال الله: (لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك

ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r17.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r17.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r17.claim: The root sense of rajz is successive movement; a camel called رجزاء has legs that tremble when it rises.
ZAJJAJ:v2p202/r17.anchor: وأصل الرجز في اللغة تتابع الحركات، فمن ذلك قولهم رجزاء إذا كانت ترتعد قوائمها عند قيامها

THALABI:v4p106#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v4p106#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who drinks wine in this world and does not repent will be deprived of it in the Hereafter.
THALABI:v4p106#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من شرب الخمر في الدنيا، ثم لم يتب منها حرمها

THALABI:v4p106#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس
THALABI:v4p106#2/r2.claim: A report warns that wine drinkers will be made to drink the venom of snakes and scorpions and suffer bodily degradation; it includes producers, sellers, carriers, and recipients in the same sin and says prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and umra are not accepted until repentance.
THALABI:v4p106#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة وابن عباس جميعا قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من شرب الخمر في الدنيا سقاه الله

THALABI:v4p106#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v4p106#2/r3.claim: The Prophet curses wine and those who drink, serve, sell, buy, press, transport, receive, or consume its price.
THALABI:v4p106#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه قال: أشهد أني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقول: «لعن الله الخمر وشاربها

THALABI:v4p106#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p106#2/r4.claim: The Prophet calls wine the key to every evil and urges avoiding it; the report also warns that debts cannot be settled with money in the next life, where deeds are apportioned.
THALABI:v4p106#2/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اجتنبوا الخمر فإنها مفتاح كل شر

THALABI:v4p107/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p107/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v4p107/r1.claim: The Prophet says a person who drinks wine after its prohibition is unfit for marriage, belief, intercession, or trust; if entrusted property is lost, God need not replace it.
THALABI:v4p107/r1.anchor: عن علي ابن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من شرب الخمر بعد أن حرمها الله على لساني

THALABI:v4p107/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p107/r2.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v4p107/r2.claim: The poet says he abandoned nabidh because it stains a man's reputation and opens the doors to evil.
THALABI:v4p107/r2.anchor: أنشدنا رضوان ابن أحمد الصيدلاني شعرا: تركت النبيذ لأهل النبيذ … وصرت حليفا لما عابه

THALABI:v4p107/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p107/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p107/r3.claim: Ansab are idols named for being set upright; the word has variant singular forms with different nun vowels and consonant doubling, while azlam are arrows used to divide shares.
THALABI:v4p107/r3.anchor: والميسر والأنصاب أي الأوثان، سميت بذلك لأنهم كانوا ينصبونها، واحدها: نصب بفتح النون وجزم الصاد، ونصب منهم النون مثقلا ومخففا والأزلام يعني القداح

THALABI:v4p107/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p107/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p107/r4.claim: The forbidden practices are defilement from Satan's work, which he adorns, so believers must avoid them.
THALABI:v4p107/r4.anchor: رجس من عمل الشيطان تزينه فاجتنبوه

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r1.claim: To explain a singular predicate for four coordinated things, al-Zamakhshari supplies an omitted مضاف: ‘the affair or nature of wine and the rest.’
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r1.anchor: فأجاب الزمخشري بأنه على حذف مضاف أي: إنما شأن الخمر، وكذا وكذا

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa similarly supplies ‘the action of these things’ as the omitted مضاف.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r2.anchor: وكذا قدره أبو البقاء فقال: " لأن التقدير: إنما عمل هذه الأشياء "

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r3.claim: The Sheikh says no مضاف is needed: directly calling all four things رجس is more emphatic, as in 9:28; the author calls this a good explanation.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ بعد حكايته كلام الزمخشري: " ولا حاجة إلى هذا، بل الحكم على هذه الأربعة أنفسها أنها رجس أبلغ من تقدير هذا المضاف

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r4.claim: Another Abu al-Baqa analysis makes رجس predicate of الخمر alone, with the predicates of the coordinated nouns omitted because the first supplies them.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r4.anchor: وأجاب أبو البقاء أيضا بأنه يجوز أن يكون " رجس " خبرا عن " الخمر " وحذف خبر المعطوفات لدلالة خبر الأول عليها

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r5.claim: The author notes the reverse parse is also possible: رجس could predicate the final noun, with earlier predicates omitted; 9:62 offers the parallel والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r5.anchor: قلت: وعلى هذا فيجوز أن يكون خبرا عن الآخر وحذف خبر ما قبله لدلالة خبر ما بعده عليه

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r6.claim: الأنصاب is the plural of نصب, and الأزلام was discussed earlier in the surah.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r6.anchor: والأنصاب جمع " نصب " ، وقد تقدم ذلك أول السورة والأزلام تقدمت أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r7.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines رجس as a dirty thing and also records a claimed relation of رجس/رجز to loud sound, like a roaring camel or thunderous cloud.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r7.anchor: قال الراغب: " هو الشيء القذر، رجل رجس، ورجال أرجاس " ثم قال:

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r8.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls رجس the name for what is impure from an ugly act; he relates the root to acting badly and the original رجس to loud thunder.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " وهو اسم لك ما استقذر

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r9.claim: The cited poem وكل رجاس يسوق الرجسا supplies evidence for the thunderous-sound sense of رجس.

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r10.speaker: ابن دريد
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r10.claim: Ibn Durayd distinguishes رجس as evil, رجز as punishment, and ركس as excrement or stench; he also says رجس can refer to two.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r10.anchor: وفرق ابن دريد بين الرجس والرجز والركس، فجعل الرجس: الشر، والرجز: العذاب، والركس: العذرة والنتن

SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r11.claim: The lexical survey concludes that رجس means a filthy, stinking thing, or was originally a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90/r11.anchor: فتحصل من هذا أنه اسم للشيء القذر المنتن أو أنه في الأصل مصدر.

SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r1.claim: من عمل الشيطان is nominative as an adjective of رجس.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r1.anchor: في محل رفع لأنه صفة ل " رجس "

SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r2.claim: The pronoun returns to رجس itself, so the command is to avoid the impurity predicated of the wine and other listed things; this is rhetorically stronger.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r2.anchor: والهاء في " فاجتنبوه " تعود على الرجس أي: فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي أخبر به عما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa refers the pronoun to the action, presupposing a deleted مضاف.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " إنها تعود على الفعل " يعني الذي قدره مضافا إلى الخمر وما بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise refers it to the omitted مضاف, or to engaging in the two things or something similar.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r4.anchor: وإلى ذلك نحا الزمخشري أيضا، قال:

SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r5.claim: The author prefers treating the listed things themselves as impurity because it expresses the point more emphatically.
SAMIN-DURR:5:90#2/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الأحسن أن هذه الأشياء جعلت نفس الرجس مبالغة.

ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r1.speaker: all lexicographers
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r1.claim: Khamr derives from khamara, “to conceal or obscure,” and denotes any substance that obscures the intellect and intoxicates.
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r1.anchor: According to all the lexicographers, the word khamr (derived from the verb khamara, "he concealed" or "obscured") denotes every substance the use of which obscures the intellect, i.e., intoxicates.

ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r2.claim: The prohibition covers drugs with intoxicating effects as well as alcoholic drinks.
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r2.anchor: Hence, the prohibition of intoxicants laid down in this verse comprises not merely alcoholic drinks, but also drugs which have a similar effect.

ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r3.claim: The sole exception is strict dire necessity, such as illness or bodily accident making intoxicants imperative and unavoidable, under 5:3.
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r3.anchor: The only exception from this total prohibition arises in cases of "dire necessity" (in the strictest sense of these words), as stipulated in the last sentence of verse 3 of this surah

ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r4.claim: Asad takes ansab metaphorically for idolatrous practices broadly, including saint worship, attributing magic to objects, and superstitious taboos.
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r4.anchor: This term has, I believe, been used here metaphorically, and is meant to circumscribe all practices of an idolatrous nature - like saint-worship, the attribution of "magic" properties to certain inanimate objects, the observance of all manner of superstitious taboos

ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r5.claim: For his explanation of al-azlam (“divining-arrows”), Asad directs readers to his note on 5:3.
ASAD-NOTES:5:90#n105/r5.anchor: For an explanation of the expression rendered by me as "divining of the future" (al-azlam, lit., "divining-arrows"), see note 9 on the second paragraph of verse 3 of this surah.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r3.claim: Al-Ma'idah adds “beware” and “know” after its emphatic prohibition of intoxicants and related evils; al-Taghabun has no comparable preceding prohibition, so the extra warning is unnecessary there.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#8/r3.anchor: فناسب ذلك ذكر هذه الزيادة لتأكيد التحذير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r2.claim: One occasion is Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's quarrel: after emigrants and Helpers drank and boasted, an Ansari struck Sa'd with a camel jaw and split his nose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r2.anchor: نزلت بسبب قصة سعد بن أبي وقاص حين شرب طائفة من الأنصار والمهاجرين فتفاخروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r3.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r3.claim: Another account connects the revelation to Umar's prayer for a clear explanation about wine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r3.anchor: وقيل بسبب قول عمر اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r4.claim: Another account links the revelation to the lengthy incident in which Hamza hamstrung Ali's she-camel and taunted him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r4.anchor: وقيل بسبب قصة حمزة وعلي حين عقر شارف علي وقال: هل أنتم إلا عبيد لأبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r5.claim: Some say prohibition came gradually, beginning with the ban on approaching prayer while drunk and culminating in this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r5.anchor: وقيل كان أمر الخمر ونزول الآيات بتدريج، فنزل يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r6.claim: Another account says an intoxicated Companion recited the disbelievers' sura inaccurately at Maghrib; drinking-related incidents then led to prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r6.anchor: وقيل بسبب قراءة بعض الصحابة وكان منتشيا في صلاة المغرب قل يا أيها الكافرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says two Ansari clans became drunk and disorderly; when sober, each saw bruises and blamed the other, creating enmity that prompted the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت بسبب حيين من الأنصار ثملوا وعربدوا فلما صحوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r8.claim: The verse follows the order to consume lawful good provisions and not forbid lawful things without sin; it addresses wine and gambling, the pleasures people valued most.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r8.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه لما أمر تعالى بأكل ما رزقهم حلالا طيبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r9.claim: People defended wine as relieving worry, energizing and emboldening drinkers, and prompting generosity, and gambling as increasing wealth and giving the pleasure of victory; the verse exposes the greater harms of those pleasures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r9.anchor: وكانوا يقولون الخمر تطرد الهموم وتنشط النفس وتشجع الجبان وتبعث على المكارم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r10.claim: A pre-Islamic poet praises a trusted brother for not wasting his wealth on wine, though his generosity can exhaust his money; Abu Hayyan uses the verse to note wine's ruinous cost.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r10.anchor: فقال: أخي ثقة لا تتلف الخمر ماله ... ولكنه قد يهلك المال نائله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r11.claim: Wine destroys reason and wealth and leads to murder, intense hatred, and sins, since reason restrains these evils; gambling takes wealth wrongfully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r11.anchor: وتنشأ عنها مفاسد أخر من قتل النفس وشدة البغضاء وارتكاب المعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r12.claim: The address is to believers and the prohibited things were entrenched desires and habits; wine was not yet forbidden, with its prohibition following Uhud in 3 AH.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r12.anchor: وهذا الخطاب للمؤمنين والذي منعوا منه في هذه الآية هي شهوات وعادات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan dates the prohibition of wine to after the Battle of Uhud in the third year after the Hijra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r13.anchor: فأما الخمر فكانت لم تحرم بعد وإنما نزل تحريمها بعد وقعة أحد سنة ثلاث من الهجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r14.claim: If ansab are sacrificial stones, calling them filth removes any lingering reverence among weak believers; if they are idols, the grouping emphasizes avoiding them like idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r14.anchor: وأما الأنصاب فإن كانت الحجارة التي يذبحون عندها وينحرون فحكم عليها بالرجس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r15.claim: The azlam were lots; most people used one marked “no” and another marked “yes.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p355#2/r15.anchor: وأما الأزلام التي كان الأكثرون يتخذونها في أحدها لا وفي الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r1.claim: Khamr is an intoxicant made from grape juice, or more broadly any drink that overwhelms and covers the intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r1.anchor: وهو المسكر المتخذ من عصير العنب أو كل ما يخامر العقل ويغطيه من الأشربة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to explain khamr broadly as any drink that overwhelms the intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r2.anchor: كل ما يخامر العقل ويغطيه من الأشربة وروي هذا عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r3.claim: Maysir is gambling, played with such implements as walnuts and dice.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r3.anchor: وهو القمار وعدوا من الله بالجوز والكعاب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r4.claim: Anṣāb are idols erected for worship; some distinguish them from fashioned idols as unshaped stones used for worship and sacrifice.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r4.anchor: وهي الأصنام المنصوبة للعبادة وفرق بعضهم بين الانصاب والاصنام بأن الانصاب حجارة لم تصور

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r5.claim: Some say anṣāb were unshaped stones erected for worship and sacrifice, while aṣnām were formed objects worshipped besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r5.anchor: وفرق بعضهم بين الانصاب والاصنام بأن الانصاب حجارة لم تصور كانوا ينصبونها للعبادة ويذبحون عندها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r6.claim: Azlām are divining arrows; al-Ālūsī says their fuller discussion has already appeared.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r6.anchor: وهي القداح وقد تقدم الكلام في ذلك على أتم وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r7.claim: Rijs means filth or impurity that sound reason finds repugnant.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines rijs as anything abominable arising from a wicked deed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r8.anchor: وعن الزجاج الرجس كل ما استقذر من عمل قبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r9.claim: The root sense is a loud sound; a rain cloud is called rajās because of its thunder, and some treat rijz as synonymous with rijs.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r9.anchor: وأصل معناه الصوت الشديد ولذا يقال للغمام رجاس لرعده والرجز بمعناه عند بعضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r10.speaker: ابن دريد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r10.claim: Ibn Durayd distinguishes rijs as evil, rijz as punishment, and riks as filth and stench.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r10.anchor: وفرق ابن دريد بن الرجس والرجز والركس فجعل الرجس الشر والرجز العذاب والركس العذرة والنتن

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r11.claim: The singular verbal noun can predicate of several things because it is unchanged for small and large amounts, as in the description of polytheists as najas.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r11.anchor: وافراد الرجس مع انه خبر عن متعدد لأنه مصدر يستوي فيه القليل والكير

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r12.claim: Alternative analyses make rijs predicate only of wine, with predicates for the coordinated nouns elided, or supply an omitted genitive such as their affair or use.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r12.anchor: لأنه خبر عن الخمر وخبر المعطوفات محذوف ثقة بالمذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r13.claim: The phrase is an adjective of rijs in the nominative sense, meaning caused by Satan's embellishment and temptation; min may instead mark origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r13.anchor: في موضع الرفع على أنه صفة ( رجس ) أي كائن من عمله لأن مسبب من تزيينه وتسويله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds it questionable to argue that an omitted genitive removes any need for causal connection or for taking min as originative.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r14.anchor: ودعوى أنه إذا قدر المضاف لم يحتج إلى ملاحظة علاقة السببية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r15.claim: The command may refer to rijs, all the listed things by an implied qualification, their implied consumption, or Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r15.anchor: أي الرجس أو جميع ما مر بتأويل ما مر أو التعاطي المقدر أو الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r16.claim: The phrase means either hoping for success or so that abstention may bring success.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r16.anchor: أي راجين فلاحكم أو لكي تفلحوا بالاجتناب عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r17.claim: The verse emphatically prohibits wine and gambling by restriction, pairing them with idols and arrows, calling them Satanic filth, and linking avoidance to success; committing them frustrates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p15#2/r17.anchor: ولقد أكد سبحانه تحريم الخمر والميسر في هذه الآية بفنون التأكيد حيث صدرت الجملة بانما وقرنا بالاصنام والازلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r2.claim: Al-ansab are idols, named because people used to erect them; the singular has several vocalized forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r2.anchor: {والأنصاب} يعني: الأوثان، سميت بذلك لأنهم كانوا ينصبونها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r3.claim: Al-azlam are arrows used for divination; the singular is zalam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r3.anchor: {والأزلام} يعني: الأقداح التي كانوا يستقسمون بها واحدها زلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r5.claim: These things are from Satan's embellishment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p94/r6.claim: The pronoun in avoid it refers back to rijs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r1.claim: The anṣāb are idols erected for worship.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r2.claim: The author says the azlām were explained earlier in the sūra.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r3.claim: Rijs means filth that sound minds find repellent; it is singular as the predicate of wine, with predicates of the coordinated nouns omitted or an omitted genitive understood as engaging in wine and gambling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r3.anchor: قذر تعاف عنه العقول، وأفرده لأنه خبر للخمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r4.claim: These practices are attributed to Satan because they result from his enticement and embellishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r5.claim: The pronoun in the command may refer to the filth, the things just mentioned, or engaging in them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r5.anchor: الضمير للرجس أو لما ذكر أو للتعاطي

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r6.claim: Avoiding these things is the means by which the believers may attain success.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r6.anchor: لعلكم تفلحون } لكي تفلحوا بالاجتناب عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r7.claim: The prohibition is reinforced by innamā, pairing wine and gambling with idols and divining arrows, calling them filth and Satan's work, and commanding avoidance as the route to success; the next verse details their worldly and religious harms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:90/r7.anchor: أكد تحريم الخمر والميسر في هذه الآية، بأن صدر الجملة ب { إنما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r1.claim: After food comes drink; the verse identifies prohibited drinks and implies that other drinks remain permitted, paralleling the surah’s earlier prohibition following permission for cattle.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r1.anchor: ولما تم بيان حال المأكل وكان داعية إلى المشرب , احتيج

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r2.claim: The address reminds believers that faith means submission and obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r2.anchor: مذكرا لهم بما أقروا به من الإيمان الذي معناه الإذعان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r3.claim: Khamr means every intoxicant, with no distinction between a small amount and a large amount.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r3.anchor: وهي كل ما أسكر سواء فيه قليله وكثيره

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r4.claim: The other practices share religious and worldly harms, cause quarrels and loud oath-taking, and are all pagan customs; listing them reinforces that drinkers, idol sacrificers, and lot-users are alike.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r4.anchor: ما واخاها في الضرر دينا ودنيا وفي كونه سببا للخصام وكثرة اللغط المقتضي للحلف والإقسام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r5.claim: The author points back to the earlier discussion of gambling in Sūrat al-Baqara.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r5.anchor: أي الذي تقدم ذكره في البقرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r6.claim: Idol-stones and divining arrows were mentioned earlier at the beginning of this surah.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r7.speaker: البخاري
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r7.claim: Al-Bukhārī says a zalam is an arrow without feathers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r7.anchor: الزلم : القدح لا ريش له - قاله البخاري

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r8.claim: Their order pairs wine’s waste of wealth with gambling, gambling’s financial corruption with idols’ religious corruption, then manifest shirk in idol worship with the hidden shirk of divining arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r8.anchor: لما كانت الخمر غاية في الحمل على إتلاف المال , قرن بها ما يليها في ذلك وهو القمار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r9.claim: Rijs is filth deserving avoidance in every respect, whether physical or abstract and whether the impurity is sensory or conceptual.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r9.anchor: أي قذر أهل لأن يبعد عنه بكل اعتبار حتى عن ذكره سواء كان عينا أو معنى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r10.claim: The singular predicate explicitly attaches to wine; predicates for the other three items are elided and understood separately, since one collective predicate does not suffice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r10.anchor: ووحد الخبر للنص على الخمر والإعلام بأن أخبار الثلاثة حذفت وقدرت , لأنها أهل لأن يقال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r11.claim: Calling the practices Satan’s work heightens repulsion by associating them with the accursed, remote one.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p535/r11.anchor: أي المحترق البعيد , ثم صرح بما اقتضاه السياق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r1.claim: Ijtināb means deliberately keeping oneself on a side apart from the prohibited thing; the singular form follows from the preceding unified ruling.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r1.anchor: أي تعمدوا أن تكونوا عنه في جانب آخر غير جانبه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r2.claim: Success means attaining all one’s aims, which cannot be achieved while engaging in these practices.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that when wine was prohibited, there was none in Medina; another version says five kinds of drink were present, but none was grape wine.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال : ( لقد حرمت الخمر وما بالمدينة منها شيء )

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r4.speaker: عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r4.claim: From the Prophet’s pulpit, ʿUmar reports that wine prohibition covered drinks made from grapes, raisins, dates, honey, wheat, and barley, and defines wine as what veils the intellect.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r4.anchor: سمعت عمر على منبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : أما بعد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r5.claim: Anas reports that while he served date wine to Abū Ṭalḥa and others, a messenger announced prohibition; they immediately ordered the jars poured out and neither questioned nor revisited the matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r5.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : ( ما كان لنا خمر غير فضيخكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r6.claim: In another report, Anas says grape wine was scarce in Medina at prohibition and most wine was made from fresh or dried dates.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r6.anchor: وي رواية عنه : ( حرمت علينا الخمر حين حرمت وما نجد خمر الأعناب إلا قليلا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r7.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r7.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī dates the prohibition to a few days after the Battle of the Trench.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p536/r7.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : وذلك بعد غزوة الأحزاب بأيام

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r1.claim: The seeker in intense longing may swear by God's beauty and majesty for a fragment of divine approach and union, but such an oath is idle under the law of contentment and a lapse under the path of surrender; God pardons it from weakness.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الطالب الصادق عند غلبات الشوق ووجدان الذوق يقسم عليه بجماله وجلاله

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r2.claim: The seeker should instead yield to God's decrees of acceptance or rejection and approach or estrangement, preferring steady service over honor, closeness, vision, or union; this reading is cited from al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r2.anchor: أن الأولى الذوبان والجمود بحسن الرضى بحسب جريان أحكام المولى في القبول والرد والإقبال والصد

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r3.claim: An unnamed Persian poem says not to waste time: opportunity is precious and time is a sword.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r3.anchor: مكن وقت ضايع فافسوس وحيف كه فرصت عزيز ست والوقت سيف

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r4.speaker: ابن الفارض
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Farid urges decisive use of time and warns that postponing things with 'later' is a dangerous affliction.

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r5.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r5.claim: The Mathnawi verses continue the exhortation to patience amid worldly hardship and in seeking the beloved Lord.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r5.anchor: أي كه صبرت نيست از دنياي دون

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r6.claim: This is the fourth of four verses revealed about wine; Bursevī says its fuller discussion occurred in al-Baqara, and wine includes every intoxicant.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r6.anchor: هذه هي الآية الرابعة من الآيات الأربع التي نزلت في الخمر وقد سبق التفصيل في سورة البقرة

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r7.claim: Maysir means every kind of gambling, including backgammon, chess, fourteen-piece games, dice, and gambling with an egg.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r7.anchor: القمار كله فيدخل فيه النرد والشطرنج والأربعة عشر

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r8.claim: Anṣāb are idols set upright for worship; the singular is naṣb, with an open nūn and still ṣād.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r8.anchor: أي الأصنام المنصوبة للعبادة واحدها نصب بفتح النون وسكون الصاد

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r9.claim: Azlām are divining arrows marked with commands, prohibitions, or left blank; pre-Islamic Arabs drew them at the Kaaba before travel, war, or trade, repeating a blank draw to learn their allotted fortune.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r9.anchor: هي سهام مكتوب على بعضها أمرني ربي وعلى بعضها نهاني ربي يطلبون بها علم ما قسم من الخير والشر

BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r10.claim: Rijs is filth that sound reason finds repugnant.
BURSEVI:v2p347#3/r10.anchor: قذر يعاف عند العقول أي تكرهه وتنفر منه العقول السليمة

BURSEVI:v2p348/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p348/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p348/r1.claim: Najās is usually what nature finds filthy, while rijs is more often what reason finds filthy; these sins are called rijs because they must be avoided like repulsive filth.
BURSEVI:v2p348/r1.anchor: والرجس بمعنى النجس إلا أن النجس يقال في المستقذر طبعا والرجس أكثر ما يقال في المستقذر عقلا

BURSEVI:v2p348/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p348/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p348/r2.claim: This phrase describes rijs as arising from Satan's work of embellishing it, urging it, and making it attractive to its perpetrators.
BURSEVI:v2p348/r2.anchor: صفة لرجس أي رجس كائن من عمله أي من تزيينه لأنه هو الداعي إليه

BURSEVI:v2p348/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p348/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p348/r3.claim: The command means to keep away from this impurity; its apparent force is obligation, with success hoped for through avoidance.
BURSEVI:v2p348/r3.anchor: أمر بالاجتناب وهو تركه جانبا وظاهر الأمر على الوجوب

BURSEVI:v2p348/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p348/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p348/r8.claim: Wine and gambling receive special emphasis because believers are being addressed and their prohibition is the main purpose; adding idols and divining arrows heightens censure by grouping four similarly harmful practices.
BURSEVI:v2p348/r8.anchor: وتخصيص الخمر والميسر تنبيها على أنهما المقصودان بالبيان لأن هذه الآية خطاب مع المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v3p157/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra relates the staged prohibition: 2:219, then 4:43 after a drunken prayer, then 5:90. Concern for deceased drinkers is answered by 5:93; the Prophet says people would have quit if it had been forbidden earlier.
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال حرمت الخمر ثلاث مرات قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يشربون الخمر ويأكلون الميسر

DURR-FULL:v3p157/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts three stages: 2:219, followed by 4:43 when people said they would avoid wine near prayer, and finally this verse, when the Prophet declared wine forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: نزل في الخمر ثلاث آيات فأول شيء نزل {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر}

DURR-FULL:v3p157/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r3.claim: Saʿd says wine prohibition was revealed after an Anṣārī hosted a meal where he and others ate and drank until intoxicated.
DURR-FULL:v3p157/r3.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: في نزل تحريم الخمر صنع رجل من الأنصار طعاما فدعانا فأتاه ناس فأكلوا وشربوا حتى انتشوا من الخمر

DURR-FULL:v3p158/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r1.claim: In Saʿd's account, intoxicated guests argued over whether Anṣār or Quraysh were better; a man struck his nose with a camel jawbone, after which he told the Prophet and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r1.anchor: وذلك قبل أن تحرم الخمر فتفاخروا فقالت الأنصار: الأنصار خير وقالت قريش: قريش خير فأهوى رجل بلحي جزور فضرب على أنفي ففزره

DURR-FULL:v3p158/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r2.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r2.claim: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh says the first prohibition came after Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and companions drank, fought, and broke Saʿd's nose.
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r2.anchor: من طريق ابن شهاب أن سالم بن عبد الله حدثه

DURR-FULL:v3p158/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r3.claim: Saʿd says three revelations concerned him: the wine prohibition after an altercation, the command to honor parents, and the rule to give charity before private counsel, later eased after his small offering.
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r3.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال نزلت في ثلاث آيات من كتاب الله نزل تحريم الخمر نادمت رجلا فعارضته وعارضني

DURR-FULL:v3p158/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says two Anṣārī tribes drank, fought, and blamed one another, breeding enmity; when critics objected that deceased Badr and Uḥud fighters had drunk, 5:93 absolved earlier consumption.
DURR-FULL:v3p158/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إنما نزل تحريم الخمر في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار شربوا فلما أن ثمل القوم عبث بعضهم ببعض

DURR-FULL:v3p159/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r1.speaker: بريدة
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r1.claim: Burayda says that after the prohibition was revealed he recited it to his drinking companions; they drained the remaining cups, poured out their wine, and declared they had stopped.
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r1.anchor: عن بريدة قال بينما نحن قعود على شراب لنا ونحن نشرب الخمر جلاء إذ قمت حتى آتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأسلم عليه

DURR-FULL:v3p159/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet first hinted to Medina's people that a ruling about wine might come, then announced its prohibition and ordered holders not to drink it.
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا أهل المدينة إن الله يعرض عن الخمر تعريضا لا أدري لعله سينزل فيها أمر

DURR-FULL:v3p159/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ reports that ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn had already renounced wine in pre-Islamic times because intoxication clouded reason and could lead to unwanted marriages; he lamented losing it when the verse was recited.
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط قال: زعموا أن عثمان بن مظعون حرم الخمر في الجاهلية وقال: لا أشرب شيئا يذهب عقلي

DURR-FULL:v3p159/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr describes the progression from 2:219, when some drank for its benefits and others abstained, through 4:43, when some only avoided prayer-time drinking, to this verse, after which ʿUmar and others quit despite lingering cravings.
DURR-FULL:v3p159/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال لما نزلت في البقرة {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس}

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r1.claim: Umar says wine was prohibited when made from barley, wheat, grapes, dates, or honey, and defines wine as anything that overwhelms the intellect.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن عمر قال : نزل تحريم الخمر وهي تصنع من خمس من الشعير والحنطة ومن العنب والتمر والعسل ، والخمر ما خامر العقل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says khamr is so named because its clear part is strained off and its sediment settles.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال : انما سميت الخمر لانها صفا صفوها وسفل كدرها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says this verse is also in the Torah, where God sends truth to abolish play, music and dancing, instruments, songs, and wine.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال : ان هذه الاية التي في القران يا ايها الذين امنوا انما الخمر والميسر والانصاب والازلام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports God's oath that anyone who drinks wine after its prohibition will be made thirsty on Judgment Day, while one who leaves it will drink in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r4.anchor: اقسم الله بيمينه وعزه من شربها بعد ما حرمت لاعطشنه يوم القيامة .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r5.claim: The Prophet warns against marked dice used for divination, calling them maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اجتنبوا هذه الكعاب المرسومة التي يزجر بها زجرا فانها من الميسر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r6.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r6.claim: Abdullah calls marked dice the Persians' maysir; similar views are reported from Ali, Ibn Umar, and Aisha.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله قال : اياكم وهذه الكعاب الموسومات فانها ميسر العجم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r7.claim: Ibn Umar defines maysir as gambling.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1196/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : الميسر هو القمار

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas defines maysir as gambling, practiced in pre-Islamic times until God prohibited that reprehensible conduct.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قوله : الميسر . قال : القمار ، كانوا يتقامرون في الجاهلية إلى مجيئ الاسلام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وطاوس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r2.claim: Sufyan transmits from Mujahid, Ata, and Tawus, perhaps only two of them, that every kind of gambling is maysir, including children's play with walnuts; Rashid ibn Sa'd and Damra ibn Habib add dice and eggs.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد وعطاء وطاوس قال سفيان : أو اثنين منهم قالوا : كل شيء من القمار فهو في الميسر حتى لعب الصبيان بالجوز

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r3.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r3.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad says anything that distracts from remembering God and from prayer is maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r3.anchor: قال : سئل القاسم بن محمد عن النرد اهي في الميسر فقال : كل ما الهى عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهو الميسر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r4.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says chess is maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب انه كان يقول

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r5.speaker: أبو الأعرج
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r5.claim: Abu al-A'raj defines maysir as casting lots with arrows over wealth and crops.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r5.anchor: عن ابن شهاب ابى الاعرج قال : الميسر الضرب بالقدح على الاموال والثمار

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says the pre-Islamic maysir of his people included exchanging meat for one or two sheep.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r6.anchor: عن داود بن الحصين انه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول : كان ميسر اهل الجاهلية بيع اللحم بالشاة والشاتين

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the ansab as stones to which people sacrificed; Mujahid, Ata, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi ibn Anas, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r7.anchor: عن عطا عن عبد الله بن عباس قال : الانصاب حجارة كانوا يذبحون لها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the azlam as arrows used to divide up matters; al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata, Ibrahim, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1197/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : والازلام قال : والازلام قداح كانوا يقتسمون بها اللامور

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the azlam were pebbles used to cast lots when someone considered going on a campaign or staying; al-Thawri is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : والازلام قال : كانت لهم حصيات اذا اراد احدهم ان يغزو أو يجلس استقسم بها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes two divining arrows, one marked that God commands and the other that He forbids; people acted or refrained according to the draw.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : الازلام يعني

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rijs as divine displeasure or wrath.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : رجس يقول : سخط

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the phrase refers to the listed wine, gambling, sacrificial stones, and divining arrows.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : رجس من عمل الشيطان يعني : انما يعني ما ذكر من الخمر والميسر والانصاب والازلام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam defines rijs as evil from Satan's work.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r5.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم يقول في قوله : رجس من عمل الشيطان قال الرجس : الشر من عمل الشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains from Satan's work as meaning produced by Satan's embellishment.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : من عمل الشيطان يعني من تزيين الشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r7.claim: Ibn Umar reports a gradual sequence of three wine verses: first the question about wine and gambling, after which people asked to keep benefiting from it and the Prophet remained silent.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1198/r7.anchor: سمعت ابن عمر يقول : نزلت في الخمر ثلاث آيات ، فاول شيئ نزل يسالونك عن الخمر والميسر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r1.claim: In Ibn Umar's account, the prayer restriction came next; people said they would avoid wine near prayer, then the final verse was revealed and the Prophet declared wine prohibited.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r1.anchor: ثم نزلت هذه الاية لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى ، فقيل : حرمت الخمر ؟ فقالوا يا رسول الله انا لا نشربها قرب الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says this is the prohibition of wine: God forbids it by commanding its avoidance, as He commands avoidance of the abomination of idols.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه فهذا تحريمهن كما قال الله فاجتنبوا الرجس من الاوثان

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains la'allakum as meaning so that you may prosper.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله الله لعلكم تفلحون يعني لكي تفلحون

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرطبي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi explains the phrase as hoping that you may meet God tomorrow.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرطبي لعلكم تفلحون يقول لعلكم غدا اذا لقيتموني

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says success means escaping the punishment God warned against and attaining the reward He promised.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1199/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق لعلكم تفلحون اي لعلكم ان تنجوا مما حذركم الله به من عذابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r1.claim: The commonly held chronology dates wine's prohibition to year three after the battle of Uhud, so this verse was revealed before al-Maida and placed there later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r1.anchor: والمشهور أن الخمر حرمت سنة ثلاث من الهجرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r2.claim: Muslim transmits Saʿd's account that before prohibition he drank at an Ansar gathering, argued that the Muhajirun were better, was struck with a camel's jawbone and wounded at the nose, then reported the incident before the verse came down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r2.anchor: روى مسلم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r3.claim: Abu Dawud transmits Ibn Abbas's report that 4:43 and 2:219 were superseded by the final prohibition in al-Maida.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r3.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن ابن عباس قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p22/r4.claim: The law introduced the ban gradually and considerately: first 2:219 acknowledged benefits but said the sin outweighed them, then 4:43 restricted drinking around prayer, and finally this verse barred wine and related practices as satanic filth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r1.claim: Rijs means visible filth or repulsiveness and can also describe inward blame; here it denotes moral and religious foulness, as in 9:125 and 33:33.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r1.anchor: والرجس الخبث المستقذر والمكروه من الأمور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r2.claim: As a generic noun predicate, the singular rijs intensifies the description, making the four items seem identical with filth; its singular form suits a source-like predicate over several nouns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r2.anchor: وهو اسم جنس فالإخبار به كالإخبار بالمصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r3.claim: The practices are attributed to Satan because his prompting entices people to pursue them; calling their conduct Satan's work makes it repellent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r3.anchor: ومعنى كونها من عمل الشيطان أن تعاطيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r4.claim: The fāʾ marks a consequence, and the pronoun in اجتنبوه refers to rijs as a whole, gathering the four prohibited things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r4.anchor: للتفريع وقد ظهر حسن موقع هذا التفريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r5.claim: The verse offers hope of success if people avoid these prohibitions and are not persisting in other prohibitions; Ibn Ashur applies his general account of laʿalla and links 2:21.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r5.anchor: رجاء لهم أن يفلحوا عند اجتناب هذه المنهيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r6.claim: Avoiding each item means avoiding its harmful intended use: drinking wine, gambling, sacrificing at idols, and consulting divining arrows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r6.anchor: واجتناب المذكورات هو اجتناب التلبس بها فيما تقصد له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r7.claim: The command does not forbid touching or displaying the objects for inspection, identifying or preserving their historical forms, or leaving wine to ferment into vinegar, though details of the last case are disputed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p24/r7.anchor: ولا يدخل تحت هذا الاجتناب اجتناب مسها أو إراءتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.claim: The address includes all believers because these desires and customs were entrenched in pre-Islamic life and still persisted in many believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r1.anchor: الخطاب للمؤمنين جميعا، لأن هذه الأشياء شهوات وعادات قد تلبس بها في الجاهلية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.claim: Wine had not yet been prohibited at this stage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r2.anchor: فأما الخمر فكانت لم تحرم بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.claim: Gambling appealed to idle people as a game and pleasure, and it also offered some kind of benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r3.anchor: وأما الميسر ففيه قمار ولذة للفارغ من النفوس ونفع أيضا بوجه ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.claim: Anṣāb may mean stones where people sacrificed because they believed the stones had special merit, or idols worshipped and sacrificed to or beside.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r4.anchor: وأما الأنصاب وهي حجارة يذكون عندها لفضل يعتقدونه فيها، وقيل هي الأصنام المعبودة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r5.speaker: امرأة الطفيل بن عمرو الدوسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r5.claim: If the verse means sacrificial stones, the wife of al-Tufayl ibn ʿAmr asked her husband whether he feared Dhu al-Shara for the children; Dhu al-Shara was a Daws idol.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r5.anchor: وهذا كما قالت امرأة الطفيل بن عمرو الدوسي لزوجها: أتخاف على الصبية من ذي الشرى شيئا؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r6.claim: If anṣāb means idols, pairing them with these other things marks the latter’s baseness, not continuing idol reverence among believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r6.anchor: وإن كانت المرادة في هذه الآية الأصنام فإنما قرنت بهذه الأمور ليبين النقص في هذه إذ تقرن بالأصنام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r7.claim: The common azlam were three divining arrows marked “no,” “yes,” and blank; people revered them, and remnants of that practice remained in some hearts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r7.anchor: وأما الأزلام فهي الثلاثة التي كان أكثر الناس يتخذونها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r8.speaker: سراقة بن جعشم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r8.claim: The azlam were the arrows held by Suraqa ibn Jaʿsham when he pursued the Prophet during the Hijra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r8.anchor: وهي التي حبسها سراقة بن جعشم حين اتبع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في وقت الهجرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r9.claim: Fortune-telling by birds and written omens are comparable practices that people still perform.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r9.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل هو الزجر بالطير وأخذ الفأل منها في الكتب ونحوه مما يصنعه الناس اليوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r10.claim: Azlam can also mean gambling arrows, since zilm means an arrow; other arrows belonged to soothsayers and idols, including those used in the divination over ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r10.anchor: وقد يقال لسهام الميسر أزلام، والزلم السهم وكان من الأزلام أيضا ما يكون عند الكهان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others report that Quraysh kept divining arrows at the Kaʿba to settle questions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r11.anchor: وكان عند قريش في الكعبة أزلام فيها أحكام ذكرها ابن إسحاق وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd explains rijs as evil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p232#2/r12.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى أن هذه الأشياء رجس، قال ابن زيد: الرجس الشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r1.claim: Rijs can describe anything blameworthy or repugnant and can also mean punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r1.anchor: كل مكروه ذميم، وقد يقال للعذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains rijs here as divine anger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في هذه الآية رجس سخط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r3.claim: Rijs may mean stench, feces, or filth; rijz means punishment only, riks feces only, while rijs can cover both punishment and impurity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r3.anchor: وقد يقال للنتن وللعذرة والأقذار رجس، والرجز العذاب لا غير، والركس العذرة لا غير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r4.claim: The imperative to avoid these things, together with hadith texts and communal consensus, establishes prohibition; wine is forbidden by the Qurʾan’s plain sense, hadith, and consensus.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r4.anchor: واقترنت بصيغة الأمر في قوله فاجتنبوه نصوص الأحاديث وإجماع الأمة، فحصل الاجتناب في رتبة التحريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya points back to his prior discussions of wine, gambling, anṣāb, and divining by arrows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم تفسير لفظة الخمر ومعناها. وتفسير الميسر في سورة البقرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r6.speaker: أبو ميسرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r6.claim: Abu Maysara says the passage descended after ʿUmar described wine’s harms and prayed for a clear ruling; when it came, ʿUmar said, “We have stopped.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r6.anchor: فقال أبو ميسرة: نزلت بسبب عمر بن الخطاب فإنه ذكر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عيوب الخمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r7.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r7.claim: Saʿd says an Anṣari host served a feast where the guests drank until intoxicated; after boasting between Anṣar and Quraysh, an Anṣari struck Saʿd’s nose with a jawbone, and Saʿd says the verse descended about him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r7.anchor: وقال مصعب بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن أبيه سعد قال: صنع رجل من الأنصار طعاما فدعانا فشربنا الخمر حتى انتشينا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says two Anṣari tribes drank until intoxicated, fought, then blamed one another for the injuries they noticed after sobering; the resulting rancor occasioned the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزل تحريم الخمر في قبيلتين من الأنصار شربوا حتى إذا ثملوا عربدوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.claim: The prohibition came gradually: after incidents including Hamza damaging camel humps and ʿAli’s drunken misrecitation at Maghrib, the prayer restriction of 4:43 came before this final prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r9.anchor: ثم لم تزل النوازل تحزب الناس بسببها حتى نزلت هذه الآية، فحرمت بالمدينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r10.claim: The final prohibition came in Medina, where grape wine was scarce; people’s fermented drinks were made from honey, dates, raisins, wheat, or barley.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r10.anchor: فحرمت بالمدينة وخمر العنب فيها قليل، إنما كانت خمرهم من خمسة أشياء من العسل ومن التمر ومن الزبيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r11.speaker: الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r11.claim: The community agrees that both small and large quantities of pure grape wine are forbidden if it has not been heated or mixed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r11.anchor: والأمة مجمعة على تحريم القليل والكثير من خمر العنب التي لم تمسها نار ولا خالطها شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r12.speaker: أكثر الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r12.claim: Most jurists say any drink that intoxicates in a large amount is forbidden even in a small amount.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r12.anchor: وأكثر الأمة على أن ما أسكر كثيره فقليله حرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r13.speaker: أبو حنيفة وبعض فقهاء الكوفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r13.claim: Abu Hanifa and some Kufan jurists permit a non-intoxicating amount of a drink that intoxicates in quantity, provided it is not grape wine; Ibn ʿAtiyya rejects this view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r13.anchor: ولأبي حنيفة وبعض فقهاء الكوفة إباحة ما لا يسكر مما يسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r14.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r14.claim: Some infer wine’s prohibition from calling it rijs and from the description of carrion, flowing blood, and pork as rijs in 6:145; Ibn ʿAtiyya questions this inference.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p233/r14.anchor: وقد خرج قوم تحريم الخمر من وصفها برجس، وقد وصف تعالى في آية أخرى الميتة والدم المسفوح ولحم الخنزير بأنها رجس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p234/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p234/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p234/r1.claim: Ijtināb means placing a thing to the side or apart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p234/r1.anchor: والاجتناب أن يجعل الشيء جانبا أو ناحية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r1.speaker: مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r1.claim: One occasion report says Saʿd drank with migrants and Ansar before prohibition; after boasting, a man struck him with a camel jawbone and split his nose, prompting the revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r1.anchor: فجدع أنفه فأتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبره فنزلت هذه الآية رواه مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r2.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr describes an Ansari hosting Saʿd; drunken boasting and insults led the host to strike Saʿd on the head with a camel jawbone, after which Saʿd complained to the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير صنع رجل من الأنصار صنيعا فدعا سعد بن أبي وقاص فلما أخذت فيهم الخمرة افتخروا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r3.speaker: أبو ميسرة عن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r3.claim: ʿUmar repeatedly asked God for a clear ruling on wine; revelations came first in al-Baqara, then 4:43, and finally this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r3.anchor: فقال اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا فنزلت هذه الآية رواه أبو ميسرة عن عمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r4.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r4.claim: Another report says Muslims drank, fought among themselves, and spoke words displeasing to God, so this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r4.anchor: أن أناسا من المسلمين شربوها فقاتل بعضهم بعضا وتكلموا بما لا يرضاه الله من القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r5.claim: Two Ansari tribes became drunk and fought; when sober, each blamed a brother for visible injuries, breeding grudges where there had been none, and the verse came down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r5.anchor: وكانوا إخوة ليس في قلوبهم ضغائن فنزلت هذه الآية رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers back to his earlier discussions of wine and gambling in al-Baqara, idols at the start of this sūra, and divining arrows in the earlier commentary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r6.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الخمر والميسر في البقرة وذكرنا في النصب في أول هذه السورة قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines rijs as a name for anything impure or repugnant; the verbs rajisa and yarjisu or yarjusu describe doing a vile deed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج هو اسم لكل ما استقذر من عمل يقال رجس الرجل يرجس ورجس يرجس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r8.claim: With an open ra, rijs can mean a loud sound; the verse's use suggests a deed too vile to mention, rising in repugnance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p416/r8.anchor: والرجس بفتح الراء شدة الصوت فكأن الرجس العمل الذي يقبح ذكره ويرتفع في القبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r1.claim: God prohibits believers from consuming wine and maysir, which Ibn Kathir identifies as gambling.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ناهيا عباده المؤمنين عن تعاطي الخمر والميسر، وهو القمار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r2.claim: Ali says chess is a form of maysir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r2.anchor: وقد ورد عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب أنه قال: الشطرنج من الميسر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r3.speaker: عطاء، مجاهد، طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r3.claim: Ata, Mujahid, and Tawus say every form of gambling is maysir, even children's play with walnuts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r3.anchor: عن عطاء ومجاهد وطاوس -قال سفيان: أو اثنين منهم-قالوا: كل شيء من القمار فهو من الميسر، حتى لعب الصبيان بالجوز.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r4.speaker: راشد بن سعد، حمزة بن حبيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r4.claim: Rashid ibn Saʿd and Hamza ibn Habib include dice, walnuts, and the eggs children play with under maysir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r4.anchor: وروي عن راشد بن سعد وحمزة بن حبيب (2) وقالا حتى الكعاب، والجوز، والبيض التي (3) تلعب بها الصبيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r5.claim: Ibn Umar defines maysir as gambling.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r5.anchor: وقال موسى بن عقبة، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر قال: الميسر هو القمار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas defines maysir as gambling and says Arabs continued gambling into Islam until God forbade these reprehensible practices.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس قال: الميسر هو القمار، كانوا يتقامرون في الجاهلية إلى مجيء الإسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says pre-Islamic maysir was selling meat in exchange for one or two sheep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r7.anchor: وقال مالك، عن داود بن الحصين: أنه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول: كان ميسر أهل الجاهلية بيع اللحم بالشاة والشاتين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r8.speaker: الأعرج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r8.claim: Al-Aʿraj defines maysir as casting arrows to stake wealth and produce.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r8.anchor: وقال الزهري، عن الأعرج قال: الميسر والضرب بالقداح على الأموال والثمار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r9.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r9.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad defines maysir as anything that distracts from remembering God and prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r9.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد: كل ما ألهى عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة، فهو من الميسر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r10.claim: A report from Abu Musa says to avoid marked dice used for divination because they are maysir; Ibn Kathir grades this report gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r10.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "اجتنبوا هذه الكعاب الموسومة التي يزجر بها زجرا فإنها من الميسر". حديث غريب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the marked dice here to mean nard, or backgammon, which is also addressed in hadith reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r11.anchor: وكأن المراد بهذا هو النرد، الذي ورد في الحديث به في صحيح مسلم، عن بريدة بن الحصيب الأسلمي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r12.claim: A sound Muslim report from Burayda says that playing nardashir is like staining one's hand with pig flesh and blood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r12.anchor: عن بريدة بن الحصيب الأسلمي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من لعب بالنردشير فكأنما صبغ يده في لحم خنزير ودمه".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r13.claim: A report from Abu Musa says whoever plays nard has disobeyed God and His Messenger.
