IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r13.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من لعب بالنرد فقد عصى الله ورسوله".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r14.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r14.claim: The nard report is also transmitted as Abu Musa's own statement rather than as prophetic speech; Ibn Kathir leaves its status uncertain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p178/r14.anchor: وروي موقوفا عن أبي موسى من قوله، فالله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r1.claim: Abu Bakra reports the Prophet's comparison: someone who plays nard and then prays is like someone who performs ablution with pus and pig blood and then prays.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r1.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "مثل الذي يلعب بالنرد، ثم يقوم فيصلي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says chess is worse than nard.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r2.anchor: وأما الشطرنج فقد قال عبد الله بن عمر: إنه شر من النرد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls Ali's view that chess is maysir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r3.anchor: وتقدم عن علي أنه قال: هو من الميسر،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r4.speaker: مالك، أبو حنيفة، أحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r4.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, and Ahmad explicitly rule chess forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r4.anchor: ونص على تحريمه مالك، وأبو حنيفة، وأحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r5.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi regards chess as disliked rather than explicitly forbidden.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عطاء، سعيد بن جبير، الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r6.claim: These authorities say ansab were stones at which sacrificial animals were slaughtered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r6.anchor: وأما الأنصاب، فقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، وغير واحد: هي حجارة كانوا يذبحون قرابينهم عندها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عطاء، سعيد بن جبير، الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r7.claim: The same authorities say azlam were arrows used for drawing lots.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179/r7.anchor: وأما الأزلام فقالوا أيضا: هي قداح كانوا يستقسمون بها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the impurity as divine displeasure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: أي سخط من عمل الشيطان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains rijس as sin.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the impurity as evil from Satan’s work.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r3.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: أي شر من عمل الشيطان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r4.claim: The pronoun refers back to the impurity; the command means to leave it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r4.anchor: الضمير عائد على الرجس، أي اتركوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r5.claim: The promise of success is encouragement to comply with the command.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra recounts the staged ban: first 2:219, then 4:43 after an intoxicated prayer leader recited confusedly, and finally this verse, after which people stopped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: حرمت الخمر ثلاث مرات، قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r8.claim: When asked about believers who died before the final prohibition while drinking and gambling, 5:93 was revealed; the Prophet said they would have left it had it been forbidden to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p179#2/r8.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: {ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at the conquest a Thaqafī or Dawsī friend brought the Prophet wine; the Prophet said its prohibition also forbids its sale, and it was poured out.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r1.anchor: سألت ابن عباس عن بيع الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r2.speaker: تميم الداري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r2.claim: Tamīm al-Dārī’s annual wine gift was rejected after the ban; the Prophet cursed Jews for melting forbidden fat to sell it and said wine and its price are forbidden. A second route is given through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p181/r2.anchor: عن تميم الداري أنه كان يهدي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم راوية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r1.speaker: قيس بن سعد بن عبادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r1.claim: The Prophet is reported to have forbidden wine, kubah, and qinīn, and warned against ghubayrāʾ, which he called a third of the world’s wine.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r1.anchor: عن قيس بن سعد بن عبادة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن ربي تبارك وتعالى حرم علي الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet lists wine, gambling, mizr, kubah, and qinīn as forbidden, and adds that witr prayer was specially given to him; Yazīd explains qinīn as lutes. Aḥmad alone reports it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله حرم على أمتي الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r3.claim: The Prophet warns against attributing words to him falsely, says wine, gambling, kubah, and ghubayrāʾ are forbidden, and declares every intoxicant unlawful; Aḥmad alone reports it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من قال علي ما لم أقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that wine is cursed in ten roles: its drinker, server, seller, buyer, presser, commissioner, carrier, recipient, and one who consumes its price, as well as wine itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r4.anchor: ابن عمر يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لعنت الخمر على عشرة وجوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts the Prophet cutting open wine containers at the market and cursing wine and those involved in its production, sale, transport, service, and price.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p183/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن عمر يقول: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المربد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r1.claim: The Prophet had Ibn ʿUmar sharpen a blade, then ordered him and companions to cut every wine container in Medina’s markets, including imported wine.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r1.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن آتيه بمدية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās rules that wine and its price are forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r2.anchor: ابن عباس، فسألته عن الخمر وثمنها، فقال: هي حرام وثمنها حرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that if another scripture and prophet were to follow this Qurʾān and Prophet, this community would have received the same severe prohibition as earlier peoples; its matter is deferred to Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r3.anchor: ثم قال ابن عباس، رضي الله عنه: يا معشر أمة محمد، إنه لو كان كتاب بعد كتابكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts the Prophet gathering and identifying wine, cursing all ten parties connected to it, then puncturing the skins despite their usefulness because he acted in anger at God’s displeasure; he refused ʿUmar’s offer to do it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p184/r4.anchor: قال ثابت: فلقيت عبد الله بن عمر فسألته عن ثمن الخمر، فقال: سأخبرك عن الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r1.claim: A wine carrier from Khaybar asks whether he may return his stock or give it away after the ban; the Prophet refuses both, and the man pours it out. Ibn Kathīr calls this report gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r2.claim: When the carrier says orphans in his care own some of the wine, the Prophet promises replacement from Bahrain’s funds when they arrive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r3.claim: The Prophet allows people to use the wine vessels by untying their openings; the wine is emptied into a valley.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r3.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان رجل يحمل الخمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r4.claim: Abū Ṭalḥa asks about orphans who inherited wine; the Prophet orders it poured out and refuses the suggestion to turn it into vinegar. The report is also transmitted by Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Tirmidhī.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p186/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك؛ أن أبا طلحة سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أيتام في حجره ورثوا خمرا فقال: "أهرقها"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr grades the preceding report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr about the verse’s Torah parallel as having a sound chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح. حديث آخر: قال عبد الله بن وهب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r2.claim: A report says that missing prayer while drunk once is like losing the world; doing so four times merits the clay of ruin, explained as the extract of Hell’s inhabitants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من ترك الصلاة سكرا مرة واحدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r3.claim: The Prophet is reported to say every fermented drink is wine and every intoxicant forbidden; intoxication reduces prayer for forty mornings, and after a fourth offense merits Hell’s pus. He also threatens whoever gives intoxicants to a young child.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r3.anchor: عن طاوس، عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "كل مخمر خمر، وكل مسكر حرام، ومن شرب مسكرا بخست

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that a person who drinks wine and does not repent will be deprived of it in the afterlife; another report says an unrepentant addict who dies will not drink it there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r4.anchor: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من شرب الخمر في الدنيا، ثم لم يتب منها حرمها في الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r5.claim: The Prophet says God will not look on Judgment Day at one disobedient to parents, an addicted wine drinker, or a person who boasts of gifts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p187/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن يسار؛ أنه سمع سالم بن عبد الله يقول: قال عبد الله بن عمر: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ثلاثة لا ينظر الله إليهم يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r1.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says that a boastful giver, a person disobedient to parents, and a wine addict will not enter Paradise; Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يدخل الجنة منان ولا عاق، ولا مدمن خمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r2.claim: Another report says Paradise is barred to one disobedient to parents, a wine addict, a boastful giver, and a child of zina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يدخل الجنة عاق، ولا مدمن خمر، ولا منان، ولا ولد زنية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r3.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r3.claim: Al-Bukhārī notes uncertain links in the report’s chain: no known hearing between Jabān and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, Salim and Jabān, or Nabit and Jabān; Ibn Kathīr notes versions through Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r3.anchor: وقال البخاري: لا يعرف لجابان سماع من عبد الله، ولا لسالم من جابان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r4.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r4.claim: ʿUthmān warns that wine is the mother of abominations, recounting how an ascetic, lured into a woman’s home, drank wine and then committed adultery and murder; wine and faith cannot long coexist.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p188/r4.anchor: وقال الزهري: حدثني أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام، أن أباه قال: سمعت عثمان بن عفان

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r7.claim: Khamr is linked to covering: wine mixes with and veils the intellect; the root also denotes whatever covers.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r7.anchor: الخمر قيل: أصله التغطية فسميت الخمر لمخامرتها العقل

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r8.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r8.claim: Al-Khalīl calls wine a familiar substance and associates its derivation with fermentation and boiling.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r8.anchor: قال الخليل: الخمر معروفة، واختارها إدراكها وغليانها

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r9.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says wine was named because it was left to ferment, changing its smell.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: سميت بذلك لأنها تركت فاختمرت، واختمارها تغير ريحها

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r10.claim: The root appears in covering vessels, a woman's khimār, a crowd, and covered dough, tying these uses to concealment.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r10.anchor: ومنه قوله: خمروا آنيتكم أي غطوها، ومنه خمار المرأة

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r11.claim: In Arabic, sorrow may be said to mix with someone, while concealing testimony is also expressed with the kh-m-r root.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r11.anchor: ويقال: خامره الحزن خالطه، وخمر شهادته كتمها

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r12.claim: Maysir means gambling and is derived from yusr, ease, the opposite of difficulty.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r12.anchor: والميسر: القمار مأخوذ من اليسر، خلاف العسر

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r13.speaker: الأزهري
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r13.claim: Al-Azharī says maysir first named the camel gambled over, divided into portions; the butcher was a yāsir because he apportioned meat.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r13.anchor: قال الأزهري: الميسر: الجزور. الذي كانوا يتقامرون عليه، سمي ميسرا لأنه يجزأ أجزاء

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r14.claim: One explanation identifies al-anṣāb as idols erected for worship.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r14.anchor: الأنصاب قيل: الأوثان سميت بذلك لأنها كانت تنصب للعبادة لها

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r15.claim: Abū Muslim identifies al-anṣāb as stones where sacrifices were made for idols.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r15.anchor: وقيل: هي الحجارة التي كانوا يذبحون عندها للأصنام، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r16.claim: The word derives from standing upright; its singular is naṣb, with the source noting pronunciations with either vowel on the nūn and light or doubled ṣād.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r16.anchor: وأصله الانتصاب، وهو القيام، نصب ينصب نصبا

JISHUMI:v3p2072/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r17.claim: Azlām are divining arrows marked 'do' or 'do not'; people followed the result for travel, residence, and other matters.
JISHUMI:v3p2072/r17.anchor: الأزلام: القداح، واحدها: زلم وزلم، وهي سهام كانوا يجعلون عليها علامات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r1.claim: The prohibition is emphatic because the sentence opens with innamā.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r1.anchor: منها تصدير الجملة بإنما ومنها أنه قرنهما بعبادة الأصنام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r2.claim: Wine and gambling are paired with idol worship to intensify their prohibition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r2.anchor: ومنها أنه قرنهما بعبادة الأصنام ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r3.claim: The Prophet likens a wine drinker to an idol worshipper; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r3.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 365 ( شارب الخمر كعابد الوثن )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r4.claim: The association with idols echoes the command to avoid the filth of idols.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r5.claim: Calling them satanic works emphasizes the prohibition because Satan produces nothing but sheer evil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r5.anchor: ومنها أنه جعلهما من عمل الشيطان والشيطان لا يأتي منه إلا الشر البحت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r6.claim: The direct command to avoid them is another emphasis of the prohibition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r6.anchor: ومنها أنه أمر بالاجتناب ومنها أنه جعل الاجتناب من الفلاح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r7.claim: Since avoidance is identified with success, committing these acts entails failure and ruin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r7.anchor: إذا كان الاجتناب فلاحا كان الارتكاب خيبة ومحقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r8.claim: Their harms include hostility and hatred among drinkers and gamblers, diversion from remembering God, and neglect of prayer times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p707#2/r8.anchor: وقوع التعادي والتباغض من أصحاب الخمر والقمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to an omitted noun such as wine and gambling, their consumption or practice, or something similar.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r2.anchor: إلى المضاف المحذوف كأنه قيل إنما شأن الخمر والميسر أو تعاطيهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r3.claim: Idols and divining arrows are grouped with wine and gambling to stress that all are pre-Islamic practices of polytheists and must be avoided.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r3.anchor: وذكر الأنصاب والأزلام لتأكيد تحريم الخمر والميسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r4.claim: After grouping all four practices, the verse singles out wine and gambling to show they are its central targets.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p708/r4.anchor: ثم أفردهما بالذكر ليرى أن المقصود بالذكر الخمر والميسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r1.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's report from Abu Maysara, Umar asks for a clear ruling on wine: 2:219 is revealed, then 4:43 bars prayer while drunk, then 5:90–91 arrives and Umar says they have stopped.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r1.anchor: ما روى ابن إسحاق عن أبي ميسرة قال : قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r2.speaker: مصعب بن سعد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas after an argument over wine ended with a man striking and splitting his head with a camel jawbone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r2.anchor: أنها نزلت في سعد بن أبي وقاص وقد لاحى رجلا على شراب , فضربه الرجل بلحي جمل , ففزر قاله مصعب بن سعد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r3.claim: The verse was revealed after two Anṣari clans became drunk and acted against one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r3.anchor: أنها نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار ثملوا من الشراب فعبث بعضهم ببعض , فأنزل الله تعالى فيهم هذه الآية , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r5.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r5.claim: The majority identify the anṣāb as idols that are worshipped.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r6.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r6.claim: Muqatil says the anṣāb are stones around the Kaaba at which sacrifices were made.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r6.anchor: أنها أحجار حول الكعبة يذبحون لها , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r7.claim: Al-azlam are wooden arrows used to draw lots or seek an omen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r7.anchor: وأما { الأزلام } فهي قداح من خشب يستقسم بها على ما قدمناه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r8.claim: Rijs means forbidden; its basic sense is something filthy and prohibited, so it is used for what is unlawful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r8.anchor: { رجس } يعني حراما , وأصل الرجس المستقذر الممنوع منه , فعبر به عن الحرام لكونه ممنوعا منه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r9.claim: These acts are from Satan's work because he calls and commands people to sin and only forbids acts of obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p63/r9.anchor: أي مما يدعو إليه الشيطان ويأمر به لأنه لا يأمر إلا بالمعاصي , ولا ينهى إلا عن الطاعات .

MUJAHID:v1p203/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p203/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p203/r1.claim: Mujahid says maysir includes Persian dice, the Arabs' divining arrows, and gambling of every kind.
MUJAHID:v1p203/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال ﴿ والميسر ﴾ كعاب فارس وقداح العرب والقمار كله

MUQATIL:5:90/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r1.claim: The prohibition was revealed after Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ and the Anṣārī ʿUthbān b. Mālik drank at a meal, fought, and Saʿd sought redress from the Prophet.
MUQATIL:5:90/r1.anchor: قوله سبحانه: { يأيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر } ، نزلت فى سعد بن أبى وقاص، رضى الله عنه، وفى رجل من الأنصار،

MUQATIL:5:90/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r2.claim: Maysir means every kind of gambling.
MUQATIL:5:90/r2.anchor: { يأيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر } ، يعنى به القمار كله،

MUQATIL:5:90/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r3.claim: Anṣāb are stones that people erected and sacrificed to.
MUQATIL:5:90/r3.anchor: { والأنصاب } ، يعنى الحجارة التى كانوا ينصبونها ويذبحون لها،

MUQATIL:5:90/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r4.claim: Azlām are the two lots or arrows they used.
MUQATIL:5:90/r4.anchor: { والأزلام } ، يعنى القدحين الذين كانوا يعملون بهما،

MUQATIL:5:90/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r5.anchor: { رجس } ، يعنى إثم، { من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه }

MUQATIL:5:90/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r6.claim: “From Satan's work” means from Satan's adornment; Muqātil compares the same wording in 28:15.
MUQATIL:5:90/r6.anchor: { من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه } ، يعنى من تزيين الشيطان، ومثله فى القصص: هذا من عمل الشيطان

MUQATIL:5:90/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r7.claim: The command to avoid wine is a prohibition: avoiding the abominations of idols in 22:30 means they are forbidden, so wine is forbidden too.
MUQATIL:5:90/r7.anchor: { فاجتنبوه } ، فهذا النهى للتحريم، كما قال سبحانه: فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان [الحج: 30]،

MUQATIL:5:90/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:90/r8.claim: Laʿallakum tufliḥūn means “so that you may succeed.”

MUQATIL:5:90-93/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:90-93/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:5:90-93/r1.claim: When someone asked him, the Prophet replied that he had been told the questioner was among the people who do good.
MUQATIL:5:90-93/r1.anchor: فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم للذى سأله: " قيل لى إنك من المحسنين "

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r2.claim: Anṣāb are idols set up for worship.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r4.claim: Rijs means either impurity or something vile and repulsive.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r5.claim: These acts are attributed to Satan because he prompts them, making them as though they were his own work.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r5.anchor: ﴿ من عمل الشيطان ﴾ لأنه يحمل عليه فكأنه عمله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r6.claim: The pronoun may refer to rijs, Satan's work, all the items mentioned, or an omitted noun meaning consuming wine and gambling.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r6.anchor: ﴿ فاجتنبوه ﴾ يرجع إلى الرجس أو إلى عمل الشيطان أو إلى المذكور

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r7.claim: The prohibition is reinforced by innamā and by pairing wine and gambling with idol worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r7.anchor: أكد تحريم الخمر والميسر من وجوه حيث صدر الجملة بإنما وقرنهما بعبادة الأصنام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r8.claim: A hadith compares a wine drinker to an idol worshipper.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r8.anchor: ومنه الحديث شارب الخمر كعابد الوثن وجعلهما رجا من عمل الشيطان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r9.claim: Calling them Satan's impurity signals sheer evil, while the command to avoid them makes avoidance a path to success and indulgence a loss.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p300/r9.anchor: ولا يأنى منه إلا الشر البحت وأمر بالاجتناب وجعل الاجتناب من الفلاح

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r1.claim: The address commands all believers to abandon entrenched desires and customs inherited from the pre-Islamic period, still ingrained in many.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r1.anchor: خطاب لجميع المؤمنين بترك هذه الأشياء إذ كانت شهوات وعادات تلبسوا بها في الجاهلية وغلبت على النفوس

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya includes bird augury and taking omens from books among similar customs people still perform.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ومن هذا القبيل هوى الزجر بالطير، وأخذ الفأل في الكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r3.claim: Wine was not yet forbidden; its prohibition came in year three after Uhud, which took place in Shawwal of that year.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r3.anchor: وأما الخمر فكانت لم تحرم بعد، وإنما نزل تحريمها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r4.claim: The discussion of maysir has already appeared in the commentary on al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r4.anchor: وأما «الميسر» فقد مضى في «البقرة» القول فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r5.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r5.claim: Some say ansab means idols; others say backgammon and chess, discussed at 10:32.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r5.anchor: وأما الأنصاب فقيل: هي الأصنام. وقيل: هي النرد والشطرنج ويأتي بيانهما في سورة «يونس»

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r6.claim: Azlam are divining arrows discussed earlier in the sura; kept at the Kaaba by custodians and idol attendants, a seeker drew one to decide whether to pursue a desired matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r6.anchor: وأما الأزلام فهي القداح وقد مضى في أول السورة القول فيها. ويقال: كانت في البيت عند سدنة البيت وخدام الأصنام

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r7.claim: Wine’s prohibition came gradually because people were deeply habituated to drinking it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r7.anchor: تحريم الخمر كان بتدريج ونوازل كثيرة فإنهم كانوا مولعين بشربها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r8.claim: The first wine passage (2:219) mentions sin and benefits, meaning commercial profits; some stopped, while others kept the benefit and avoided the sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r8.anchor: يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r9.claim: After 4:43 barred prayer while drunk, some stopped while others drank outside prayer until this verse made wine forbidden; some said nothing was forbidden more harshly.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r9.anchor: فتركها بعض الناس وقالوا: لا حاجة لنا فيما يشغلنا عن الصلاة، وشربها بعض الناس في غير أوقات الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r10.speaker: أبو ميسرة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r10.claim: Abu Maysara says the verses followed Umar’s account of wine’s harms and prayer for a clear ruling; Umar responded, ‘We have stopped.’
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r10.anchor: وقال أبو ميسرة: نزلت بسبب عمر بن الخطاب فإنه ذكر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عيوب الخمر، وما ينزل بالناس من أجلها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r11.claim: Abu Dawud transmits Ibn Abbas’s statement that the wine passages in 2:219 and 4:43 were abrogated by the Ma’ida prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r11.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن ابن عباس قال: { يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى } و { يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r12.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r12.claim: Saʿd says that before wine was prohibited, Ansar invited him to food and wine; after he said the Muhajirun were better, a man broke his nose with a camel jawbone, and the prohibition was revealed concerning him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91/r12.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه قال: نزلت في آيات من القرآن وفيه قال: وأتيت على نفر من الأنصار فقالوا: تعال نطعمك

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r1.claim: Reports show wine was then an accepted, undisputed practice and the Prophet did not object; 4:43 indicates drinking was allowed before the final prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r1.anchor: هذه الأحاديث تدل على أن شرب الخمر كان إذ ذاك مباحا معمولا به معروفا عندهم بحيث لا ينكر ولا يغير

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r2.claim: Hamza’s incident suggests he became intoxicated after damaging Ali’s camels; the Prophet recognized this but did not rebuke him. Hamza may have drunk quickly without intending intoxication.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r2.anchor: فعرف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه ثمل ثم إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ينكر على حمزة ولا عنفه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r3.claim: This conflicts with jurists’ claim that intoxication is forbidden in every religious law: law serves welfare, reason is its basis, and whatever destroys or clouds reason should be prohibited.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r3.anchor: وهذا خلاف ما قاله الأصوليون وحكوه فإنهم قالوا: إن السكر حرام في كل شريعة لأن الشرائع مصالح العباد لا مفاسدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rijs as divine displeasure; it can also mean stench, excrement, or filth, while rajz means punishment and riks means excrement.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: «رجس» سخط وقد يقال للنتن والعذرة والأقذار رجس.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r5.claim: ‘From Satan’s work’ means Satan incites and embellishes these acts; alternatively Satan initiated them and people followed.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r5.anchor: ومعنى { من عمل الشيطان } أي بحمله عليه وتزيينه. وقيل: هو الذي كان عمل مبادىء هذه الأمور بنفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r6.claim: Ijtanibuhu means to put it far away and set it aside.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فاجتنبوه } يريد أبعدوه واجعلوه ناحية

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r7.claim: The avoidance command, with Prophetic reports and consensus, establishes wine’s prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r7.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى باجتناب هذه الأمور، واقترنت بصيغة الأمر مع نصوص الأحاديث وإجماع الأمة، فحصل الاجتناب في جهة التحريم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r8.claim: Muslims agree al-Ma’ida revealed wine’s prohibition; it is Medinan and among the last revelations.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r8.anchor: ولا خلاف بين علماء المسلمين أن سورة «المائدة» نزلت بتحريم الخمر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r9.claim: Carrion, blood, and pork are prohibited in 6:145 declaratively, whereas wine is prohibited through command and rebuke, a stronger prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90/r9.anchor: وورد التحريم في الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير في قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when wine was prohibited the Companions told one another it was forbidden and equated with shirk because the verse coupled it with sacrifice to idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس قال: لما نزل تحريم الخمر، مشى أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعضهم إلى بعض، وقالوا حرمت الخمر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r2.claim: Tying success to the command indicates that its obligation is strongly emphasized.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r2.anchor: ثم علق { لعلكم تفلحون } فعلق الفلاح بالأمر، وذلك يدل على تأكيد الوجوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r3.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r3.claim: The majority infer ritual impurity from wine’s prohibition, its description as rijs, and the command to avoid it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r3.anchor: فهم الجمهور من تحريم الخمر، واستخباث الشرع لها، وإطلاق الرجس عليها، والأمر باجتنابها، الحكم بنجاستها.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r4.speaker: ربيعة والليث بن سعد والمزني
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r4.claim: Rabiʿa, al-Layth, al-Muzani, and some later Baghdadi and Cairene scholars consider wine pure and only drinking it forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r4.anchor: وخالفهم في ذلك ربيعة والليث بن سعد والمزني صاحب الشافعي، وبعض المتأخرين من البغداديين والقرويين فرأوا أنها طاهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن الحداد القروي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Haddad argues wine is pure because Companions poured it into Medina’s streets; if impure, they would not have done so and the Prophet would have forbidden it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r5.anchor: سعيد بن الحداد القروي على طهارتها بسفكها في طرق المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi answers that the Companions lacked wells and household latrines, and removal from town was difficult; wide roads and small avoidable spills made disposal practical and publicly demonstrated wine’s destruction.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r6.anchor: والجواب أن الصحابة فعلت ذلك لأنه لم يكن لهم سروب ولا آبار يريقونها فيها، إذ الغالب من أحوالهم أنهم لم يكن لهم كنف في بيوتهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r7.claim: Although prohibition alone does not entail impurity, rijs means filth in Arabic; requiring explicit text for every ruling would disable law, since many impurities are inferred from general texts and analogy.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r7.anchor: قلنا: قوله تعالى: «رجس» يدل على نجاستها: فإن الرجس في اللسان النجاسة، ثم لو التزمنا ألا نحكم بحكم إلا حتى نجد فيه نصا لتعطلت الشريعة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r8.claim: The command requires unrestricted avoidance: no benefit is allowed through drinking, selling, turning wine into vinegar, using it as medicine, or otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90#2/r8.anchor: يقتضي الاجتناب المطلق الذي لا ينتفع معه بشيء بوجه من الوجوه لا بشرب ولا بيع ولا تخليل ولا مداواة ولا غير ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r1.claim: The Prophet told a man who gifted him wine that the One who forbade drinking it forbade selling it; the man emptied the vessel.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r1.anchor: إن الذي حرم شربها حرم بيعها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r2.claim: The Prophet asked why the hide of a dead sheep had not been taken, tanned, and used.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r2.anchor: هلا أخذتم إهابها فدبغتموه فانتفعتم به

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r3.claim: The wine-sale report indicates there is no lawful utility in wine; had there been one, the Prophet would have explained it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r3.anchor: إذ لو كان فيها منفعة من المنافع الجائزة لبينه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r4.claim: Muslims unanimously forbid selling wine and blood; this supports forbidding sales of excrement, impurities, and inedibles.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r4.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على تحريم بيع الخمر والدم، وفي ذلك دليل على تحريم بيع العذرات

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r5.claim: Malik disliked sale of animal dung; Ibn al-Qasim permitted it for its utility, while Malik's analogy is supported by the hadith and is also the Shafi'i position.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r5.anchor: كره مالك بيع زبل الدواب، ورخص فيه ابن القاسم لما فيه من المنفعة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r6.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r6.claim: The majority of jurists prohibit anyone from treating wine to turn it into vinegar.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r6.anchor: ذهب جمهور الفقهاء إلى أن الخمر لا يجوز تخليلها لأحد

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r7.claim: If conversion were allowed, the Prophet would not have ordered the wine emptied; no one treats poured-out wine as property whose loss must be compensated.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r7.anchor: لو جاز تخليلها ما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليدع الرجل أن يفتح المزادة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r8.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r8.claim: Uthman ibn Abi al-As poured out an orphan's wine; when the Prophet was asked about converting wine to vinegar, he said no and forbade it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r8.anchor: وقد أراق عثمان بن أبي العاص خمرا ليتيم، واستؤذن صلى الله عليه وسلم في تخليلها فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r9.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي والليث بن سعد والكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r9.claim: Another group allows treating wine into vinegar and eating the result, whether conversion is by a person or otherwise.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: لا بأس بتخليل الخمر ولا بأس بأكل ما تخلل منها بمعالجة آدمي

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa permits adding musk or salt if the wine becomes a preserve and changes out of its wine-state.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إن طرح فيها المسك والملح فصارت مربى وتحولت عن حال الخمر جاز

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r11.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan disagrees about preserves: wine may not be treated except by converting it to vinegar alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r11.anchor: وخالفه محمد بن الحسن في المربى وقال: لا تعالج الخمر بغير تحويلها إلى الخل وحده

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r12.claim: The Iraqis cite a weakly transmitted report that Abu al-Darda ate wine preserve, saying sun and salt tanned it; Umar and Uthman ibn Abi al-As opposed conversion, and no opinion overrides the Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r12.anchor: احتج العراقيون في تخليل الخمر بأبي الدرداء وهو يروى عن أبي إدريس الخولاني عن أبي الدرداء من وجه ليس بالقوي

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r13.claim: The author allows that the conversion ban may have applied at Islam's beginning to end the recently established drinking habit; later consumption of converted wine would then not be barred.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r13.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المنع من تخليلها كان في بدء الإسلام عند نزول تحريمها لئلا يستدام حبسها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r14.speaker: أشهب عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r14.claim: Ashhab transmits from Malik that vinegar made by a Christian may be eaten, and the same applies if made by a Muslim, though the Muslim should seek forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r14.anchor: روى أشهب عن مالك قال: إذا خلل النصراني خمرا فلا بأس بأكله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r15.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r15.claim: The author identifies as correct Malik's report through Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb: a Muslim may neither treat wine into vinegar nor sell it, but must pour it out.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-92/r15.anchor: والصحيح ما قاله مالك في رواية ابن القاسم وابن وهب أنه لا يحل لمسلم أن يعالج الخمر حتى يجعلها خلا ولا يبيعها،

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r1.speaker: مالك وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r1.claim: Malik and his associates agree that vinegar is lawful when wine turns into it by itself; Umar, Qabisa, Ibn Shihab, Rabi'a, and one Shafi'i position agree, as does the established Shafi'i view.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r1.anchor: لم يختلف قول مالك وأصحابه أن الخمر إذا تخللت بذاتها أن أكل ذلك الخل حلال

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r2.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r2.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says wine can be owned because it can relieve choking or extinguish fire; the author says this attribution to Malik is unknown and follows only from considering wine pure.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r2.anchor: ذكر ابن خويزمنداد أنها تملك، ونزع إلى ذلك بأنه يمكن أن يزال بها الغصص، ويطفأ بها حريق

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r3.claim: The author rejects ownership: if wine could be owned, the Prophet would not have ordered it poured out, and that order negates its alleged utility.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r3.anchor: ولو جاز ملكها لما أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإراقتها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r4.claim: The verse prohibits backgammon and chess with or without stakes: amusements that draw people into more, create enmity, and distract from remembrance and prayer share wine's rationale.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r4.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على تحريم اللعب بالنرد والشطرنج قمارا أو غير قمار

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r5.claim: Although games do not intoxicate, God pairs gambling with wine and attributes enmity and distraction to both, so their shared causes support equal prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r5.anchor: قد جمع الله تعالى بين الخمر والميسر في التحريم، ووصفهما جميعا بأنهما يوقعان العداوة والبغضاء

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r6.claim: A little wine does not intoxicate yet is forbidden like a large amount; likewise chess or backgammon can be forbidden without intoxication.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r6.anchor: قليل الخمر لا يسكر كما أن اللعب بالنرد والشطرنج لا يسكر ثم كان حراما مثل الكثير

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r8.claim: The gifted wine vessel shows that its recipient had not learned the abrogating prohibition and still followed the earlier permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r8.anchor: مهدى الراوية يدل على أنه كان لم يبلغه الناسخ، وكان متمسكا بالإباحة المتقدمة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r9.claim: The author endorses the principle that a ruling is displaced for someone when the abrogation reaches them, not merely when the abrogating text exists.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r9.anchor: دليلا على أن الحكم لا يرتفع بوجود الناسخ كما يقوله بعض الأصوليين بل ببلوغه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r10.speaker: أهل قباء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r10.claim: The people of Quba continued praying toward Jerusalem until a messenger told them of the change, whereupon they turned toward the Kaaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r10.anchor: كما وقع لأهل قباء إذ كانوا يصلون إلى بيت المقدس إلى أن أتاهم الآتي فأخبرهم بالناسخ

QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r11.claim: The author notes that wine, its derivation, and gambling were discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:90-91#2/r11.anchor: وتقدم فيها ذكر الخمر واشتقاقها والميسر

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r1.claim: This third set of rulings follows the permission to enjoy lawful good things in 5:87–88 by clarifying that wine and gambling are prohibited rather than lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r1.anchor: وجه اتصاله بما قبله أنه تعالى قال فيما تقدم { لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم }

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r2.claim: One etymology says wine is called khamr because it mixes with and veils the mind.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r2.anchor: سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها خامرت العقل ، أي خالطته فسترته

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī offers another etymology: it was left to ferment and change its smell.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي : تركت فاختمرت ، أي تغير ريحها

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r4.claim: Maysir is their gambling over a camel; anṣāb are idols set up for worship; azlām are arrows marked good and bad. Rāzī points to his earlier explanations in 5:3 and Sūrat al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r4.anchor: الميسر هو قمارهم في الجزور ، والأنصاب هي آلهتهم التي نصبوها يعبدونها ، والأزلام سهام مكتوب عليها خير وشر

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r5.claim: Rāzī directs readers to his earlier discussion of anṣāb and azlām at 5:3, and of wine and gambling in Sūrat al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#2/r5.anchor: وذكرنا معنى الأنصاب والأزلام في أول هذه السورة عند قوله } وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام }

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r1.claim: Rijs means anything abominable in action; its root suggests a forceful sound, as in thunderous clouds, so it denotes conduct powerfully and completely foul.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r1.anchor: الرجس في اللغة كل ما استقذر من عمل . يقال : رجس الرجل رجسا ورجس إذا عمل عملا قبيحا

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r2.claim: Calling these things Satan’s work intensifies their ugliness: Satan and disbelievers are impure, the impure invite only to the impure, and attribution to Satan stresses extreme repugnance.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r2.anchor: كل ما أضيف إلى الشيطان فالمراد من تلك الإضافة المبالغة في كمال قبحه

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r3.claim: One grammatical reading makes the pronoun in اجتنبوه refer to rijs, whose scope covers all four prohibited things.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r3.anchor: أنها عائدة إلى الرجس ، والرجس واقع على الأربعة المذكورة

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to an omitted noun such as the conduct or handling of wine and gambling.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r4.anchor: أنها عائدة إلى المضاف المحذوف ، كأنه قيل : إنما شأن الخمر والميسر أو تعاطيهما

RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r5.claim: The next verse names worldly harms of wine and gambling: Satan seeks to create enmity and hatred between people and distract them from remembering God and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v12p66#3/r5.anchor: ذكر فيها نوعين من المفسدة : فالأول : ما يتعلق بالدنيا وهو قوله :

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r1.claim: This is the fourth and final revelation on intoxicants: after 16:67, 2:219, and 4:43, it completely prohibits wine and gambling.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r1.anchor: This is the fourth and final passage in the chronological order of revelation relating to intoxicating drinks

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r2.claim: Maysir names a specific pre-Islamic Arabian gambling game, but applies to all gambling; the wine ban extends to every intoxicant.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r2.anchor: Gambling translates maysir, a specific form of gambling popular in pre-Islamic Arabia

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r3.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r3.claim: In a sermon, ʿUmar explained khamr, technically grape wine, as what clouds the intellect; thus the ban covers any mind-clouding substance.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r3.anchor: explained by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb in a sermon in which he said

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r4.claim: The prohibition on intoxicants includes their sale and any profit from selling them.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r4.anchor: the ban on intoxicating beverages includes not only their consumption, but also their sale and any profit attained by it

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r5.claim: Some extend the gambling ban to time-wasting games such as chess and backgammon; the author says neither was legally banned and both remain popular among Muslims.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r5.anchor: Some considered the ban on gambling to extend to all games that squander people’s time fruitlessly, such as chess and backgammon

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r6.claim: Anṣāb likely refers to animal sacrifice at stone altars, a practice mentioned in 5:3 as making meat unlawful.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r6.anchor: is likely a reference to the idolatrous practice of sacrificing animals

STUDYQURAN:5:90/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r7.speaker: Companions of the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r7.claim: Accounts say the verse followed drunken Companions fighting, with one man seriously injured.
STUDYQURAN:5:90/r7.anchor: Some accounts report that the present verse was revealed after some of the Prophet’s Companions became drunk and began to fight with one another

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r1.claim: Some Companions had forbidden themselves women, sleep, and meat in imitation of priests and monks; God sent 5:87 to stop them from forbidding what He made lawful.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله فيهم على نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابه ينهاهم عن ذلك

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r3.claim: The prohibited practices are drinking wine, gambling on camels, sacrificing at altars, and drawing lots with divining arrows; abstain from all of them.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r3.anchor: إن الخمر التي تشربونها، والميسر الذي تتياسرونه، والأنصاب التي تذبحون عندها، والأزلام التي تستقسمون بها

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r4.claim: These practices are Satan's embellishment, invitation, and beautification, not deeds urged by God or pleasing to Him; God disapproves of them.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r4.anchor: من تزيين الشيطان لكم، ودعائه إياكم إليه، وتحسينه لكم، لا من الأعمال التي ندبكم إليها ربكم

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains rijis as sin and foulness that God disapproves of and detests for the believers.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r5.anchor: يقول: إثم ونتن، سخطه الله وكرهه لكم

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rijis here as God's displeasure.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {رجس من عمل الشيطان} [المائدة: 90] يقول: سخط

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses rijis as evil.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {رجس من عمل الشيطان} [المائدة: 90] قال: " الرجس: الشر "

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r8.claim: Al-Anṣāb is the plural of naṣb; he refers readers to his earlier explanation of naṣb and its poetic evidence.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r8.anchor: وأما الأنصاب، فإنها جمع نصب، وقد بينا معنى النصب بشواهده فيما مضى

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r9.claim: The command means leave these practices, reject them, and do not do them.

TAB-FULL:v8p655/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r10.claim: Success means attaining prosperity with God by abandoning these acts; al-Ṭabarī cross-references the same phrase in 2:189.
TAB-FULL:v8p655/r10.anchor: لكي تنجحوا فتدركوا الفلاح عند ربكم بترككم ذلك

TABATABAI:5:90-93/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93/r1.claim: The verses form a coherent unit, likely revealed together or close in time; they address wine, with some also treating gambling, idols, and divining arrows, and the last verse answers an objection.
TABATABAI:5:90-93/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات متلائمة سياقا فكأنها نزلت دفعة أو هي متقاربة نزولا

TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r1.claim: The prohibition developed in its mode of address—from general prohibition, to specific warning, to the prayer restriction if 4:43 concerns wine, and finally this emphatic ban—not through legal stages that imply abrogation; 7:33 and 2:219 already establish prohibition clearly.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r1.anchor: بل بمعنى أن الآيات تدرجت في النهي عنها بالتحريم على وجه عام وذلك قوله تعالى { والإثم } ثم بالتحريم الخاص

TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r2.claim: These are the latest verses prohibiting wine; their emphases include innama, calling the items filth and Satan's work, commanding avoidance, promising success, naming harms, asking whether people will desist, and warning against disobedience.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r2.anchor: فهذه الآيات آخر ما نزل في تحريم الخمر يدل على ذلك أقسام التأكيد المودعة فيها من { إنما } والتسمية بالرجس

TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r3.claim: Khamr is any fermented liquid intoxicant; maysir is gambling generally; ansab are idols or revered sacrificial stones; azlam are divining lots, as the earlier food-ban context supports.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#2/r3.anchor: فالخمر ما يخمر العقل من كل مائع مسكر عمل بالتخمير

TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r1.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r1.claim: An objection takes azlam as fortune-telling arrows: since maysir already includes lottery by cups, it asks why a specific item follows the general term; a cited line uses azlam for divining arrows.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r1.anchor: فإن قلت الميسر بعمومه يشمل الأزلام بالمعنى الآخر الذي هو الاستقسام بالأقداح

TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r2.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r2.claim: On this reading, three similar arrows marked “do,” “do not,” and blank were drawn before important acts; the blank was redrawn, and the practice sought one's allotted good or provision.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r2.anchor: أنهم كانوا يتخذون أخشابا ثلاثة رقيقة كالسهام أحدها مكتوب عليه

TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r3.claim: Al-Tabatabai prefers lottery by arrows, as 5:3's food-prohibition context supports it; without that clue the word is ambiguous and its intended sense would depend on the Sunnah.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r3.anchor: وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام } ظاهرة في الاستقسام بالأقداح الذي هو نوع من القمار

TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r4.claim: Reports from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt permit seeking guidance by rosary and similar means when one remains uncertain after thought and consultation.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r4.anchor: وقد وردت عدة أخبار من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في جواز الأخذ بالخيرة من السبحة وغيرها عند الحيرة

TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r5.claim: Istikhara asks God to resolve practical indecision after reason and qualified consultation; it neither claims hidden knowledge, shares divine governance, nor creates a binding legal ruling, but selects action or inaction.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#3/r5.anchor: كان له أن يعين ما ينبغي أن يختاره بنوع من التوجه إلى ربه

TABATABAI:5:90-91/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r1.claim: The consequences of acting or refraining after istikhara may be good or bad, just as after thought or consultation; its function is to end hesitation in choosing.
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r1.anchor: فهو كالتفكر والاستشارة طريق لقطع الحيرة والتردد في مقام العمل

TABATABAI:5:90-91/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r2.claim: Sound reports through both Sunni and Shiʿi routes say the Prophet welcomed good omens, discouraged bad omens, and taught people to proceed trusting God; this permits taking a favorable omen from scripture.
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r2.anchor: قد ورد في الصحيح من طرق الفريقين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يتفاءل بالخير ويأمر به

TABATABAI:5:90-91/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r3.claim: A person may proceed with a favorable omen or, if none appears, continue while relying on God; this only reassures the person about an action already judged promising, and al-Tabatabai rejects making azlam mean omens to ban istikhara.
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r3.anchor: فإن كان معه ما يتفأل به من الخير وإلا مضى في الأمر متوكلا على الله تعالى

TABATABAI:5:90-91/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r4.claim: Following al-Raghib's Mufradat, rijṣ means something dirty; rijasa is an aversive quality, like impurity, that makes nature recoil and avoid it.
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r4.anchor: فالرجس الشيء القذر على ما ذكره الراغب في مفرداته فالرجاسة بالفتح كالنجاسة والقذارة

TABATABAI:5:90-91/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r5.claim: These practices are called filth because they contain no lasting human good, despite the worldly benefits acknowledged in 2:219; this helps explain their attribution to Satan and the next verse's account of his divisive aims.
TABATABAI:5:90-91/r5.anchor: وليس إلا أنها بحيث لا تشتمل على شيء مما فيه سعادة إنسانية أصلا سعادة يمكن أن تصفو وتتخلص في حين من الأحيان

TABATABAI:5:90-93#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#5/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:90-93#5/r4.claim: Hisham b. Salim reports from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq that Hamza and companions drank sakarkah; Hamza slaughtered ʿAlī’s camel, prompting ʿAlī’s complaint and the prohibition’s revelation before Uḥud, where Hamza reconciled with the Prophet and was martyred.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#5/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن سالم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول بينا حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأصحاب له على شراب لهم

TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r1.claim: The Ayyashi report continues: Hamza’s shroud could not cover his whole body; ʿAlī stayed firm at Uḥud, and the Prophet embraced and kissed Hamza before sending him back into battle, where he died.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r1.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام نحو من سرياني هذا، فكان إذا غطى وجهه انكشف رجلاه

TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r2.claim: In al-Zamakhsharī’s account, prohibition came in stages: 2:219, then 4:43 after an intoxicated worshipper garbled prayer, then 5:90–91 after ʿUmar drank, struck ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf, and lamented Badr’s dead; ʿUmar then said they desisted.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r2.anchor: وعن الزمخشري في ربيع الأبرار قال أنزل في الخمر ثلاث آيات

TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r3.claim: Saʿd says an Anṣārī feast before prohibition led to drinking and tribal boasting; a man struck Saʿd’s nose with a camel jaw, after which he complained to the Prophet and this verse was revealed.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r3.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال في نزل تحريم الخمر صنع رجل من الأنصار طعاما

TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r4.claim: The many public-route accounts differ sharply; judging the Companions mentioned in them is outside this exegetical inquiry, but they support the indication that some Muslims kept drinking after 2:219 until 5:90.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#6/r4.anchor: هذه الروايات تؤيد ما ذكرناه في البيان السابق أن في الآيات إشعارا أو دلالة

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts four wine-related verses: 2:219 was followed, then 16:67, after which people drank, and finally the two verses in al-Māʾidah ending with the command to desist.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير الطبري عن الشعبي قال نزلت في الخمر أربع آيات

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the report’s apparent abrogation sequence, in which 16:67 abrogates 2:219 and al-Māʾidah then abrogates 16:67.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r3.anchor: أقول ظاهره نسخ آية النحل لآية البقرة ثم نسخ آيتي المائدة لآية النحل

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says every prophet’s mission included wine’s prohibition in God’s knowledge; wine remained forbidden, but people were gradually moved between obligations because imposing everything at once would make them abandon religion.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r4.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال ما بعث الله نبيا قط إلا وفي علم الله أنه إذا أكمل دينه كان فيه تحريم الخمر

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r5.claim: In a report from Abū Jaʿfar, the Prophet defines maysir as anything wagered on, including knucklebones and walnuts, anṣāb as sacrifices to idols, and azlām as divining arrows.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r5.anchor: قيل يا رسول الله ما الميسر؟ قال كلما تقمرت به حتى الكعاب والجوز

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar transmits the Prophetic rule that every intoxicant is forbidden and every intoxicant is wine; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes a Sunni version through Ibn ʿUmar with the wording that every wine is forbidden.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r6.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r7.claim: Reports from the Imams establish the general rules that every intoxicant is forbidden and anything used for gambling is maysir.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r7.anchor: وقد استفاضت الروايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام بأن كل مسكر حرام، وأن كلما يقامر عليه فهو ميسر

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r8.claim: Abū al-Ṣabāḥ asks Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq whether nabīdh and wine are equivalent; he says no, God forbade all wine, little or much, while the Prophet forbade intoxicating drinks, and whatever the Prophet forbids God has forbidden.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r8.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي الصباح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن النبيذ

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r9.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r9.claim: Mūsā b. Jaʿfar says wine was prohibited for its consequences, not for an intrinsic sin; anything with wine’s consequences, or that acts like wine, is classified as wine.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r9.anchor: عن موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام قال إن الله لم يحرم الخمر لإثمها ولكن حرمها لعاقبتها

TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r10.claim: Reports censuring wine and gambling from both Muslim traditions are too numerous to count; readers seeking them should consult the major hadith collections.
TABATABAI:5:90-93#7/r10.anchor: والأخبار في ذم الخمر والميسر من طرق الفريقين فوق حد الإحصاء

TABRISI:5:90-91/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r1.claim: Khamr is fermented grape juice that intoxicates in quantity; its name comes from covering the mind, as khamara means to cover or conceal.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r1.anchor: الخمر عصير العنب المشتد وهو العصير الذي يسكر كثيره وسمي خمرا لأنها بالسكر تغطي على العقل

TABRISI:5:90-91/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r2.claim: Maysir means gambling generally and is connected with making the camel’s slaughter and division easy through gambling; its root yusr means ease.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r2.anchor: والميسر القمار كله من تيسير أمر الجزور بالاجتماع على القمار فيه وأصله من اليسر خلاف العسر

TABRISI:5:90-91/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:5:90-91/r3.claim: An alternative etymology says the left hand is named optimistically for easing work, or because it assists the right and makes work easier.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r3.anchor: وقيل: لأنها تعين اليد اليمنى فيكون العمل أيسر

TABRISI:5:90-91/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r4.claim: Anṣāb are idols set upright for worship; the root also underlies standing, exertion from work requiring standing, a knife’s mounting, and standing against an enemy.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r4.anchor: والأنصاب الأصنام واحدها نصب وسمي ذلك لأنها كانت تنصب للعبادة لها والانتصاب القيام

TABRISI:5:90-91/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r5.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:5:90-91/r5.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse warns against worshipping an erected idol and the devil, illustrating naṣb as the upright idol.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r5.anchor: قال الأعشى: وذا النصب المنصوب لا تنسكنه ولا تعبد الشيطان والله فاعبدا

TABRISI:5:90-91/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r6.claim: Azlām are divining arrows used in gambling; the commentary had discussed them at the beginning of the sūra.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r6.anchor: والأزلام القداح وهي سهام كانوا يجيلونها للقمار وقد ذكرنا ما قيل فيها في أول السورة

TABRISI:5:90-91/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r7.claim: Rajz with zāy means torment; the root evokes repeated movement, as in a she-camel whose legs tremble.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r7.anchor: والرجز بالزاي هو العذاب وأصل الرجز تتابع الحركات. يقال ناقة رجزاء إذا كانت ترتعد قوائمها

TABRISI:5:90-91/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:5:90-91/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says rijs is any loathsome deed; the verb describes doing something bad, while rijs with fatḥa can mean loudness, as in loud thunder.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r8.anchor: الزجاج: الرجس في اللغة اسم لكل ما استقذر من عمل

TABRISI:5:90-91/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r9.claim: Rijs denotes what is repugnant and rises to the utmost degree of vileness.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r9.anchor: فكان الرجس الذي يقبح ذكره ويرتفع في القبح

TABRISI:5:90-91/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r10.claim: The prohibition follows preceding legal rulings and turns the audience away from pre-Islamic practices toward Islamic law.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r10.anchor: ثم عطف الله تعالى على ما بين من الأحكام بالنهي عن أفعال أهل الجاهلية والنقل عنها

TABRISI:5:90-91/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91/r11.claim: The commentary says wine and gambling were already discussed in al-Baqara.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r11.anchor: مر معناهما في سورة البقرة. قال ابن عباس:

TABRISI:5:90-91/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:5:90-91/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says khamr here means every drink that intoxicates.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد بالخمر جميع الأشربة التي تسكر

TABRISI:5:90-91/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:5:90-91/r13.claim: A report from the Prophet lists fermented drinks from honey, grapes, raisins, dates, wheat, maize, barley, and sult as wine.
TABRISI:5:90-91/r13.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " الخمر من تسع من البتع وهو العسل ومن العنب

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses maysir as gambling, which occurs in many forms.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r1.anchor: وقال في الميسر: يريد القمار وهو في أشياء كثيرة

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r2.claim: The phrase is elliptical: it means drinking or handling wine, worshipping idols, and drawing lots are defilement from Satan’s work.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r2.anchor: لا بد من أن يكون في الكلام حذف والمعنى شرب الخمر وتناوله أو التصرف فيه وعبادة الأنصاب

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r3.claim: Although these are physical things created by God, they are attributed to Satan because he urges corruption through them: intoxication removes reason, gambling cultivates base traits, idol worship entails shirk, and lots encourage poor judgment and reliance on chance.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r3.anchor: وإنما نسبها إلى الشيطان وهي أجسام من فعل الله لما يأمر به الشيطان فيها من الفساد

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r4.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r4.claim: Al-Baqir includes chess, backgammon, every kind of gambling, and even children’s gambling with walnuts under maysir.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r4.anchor: وقال الباقر ع: يدخل في الميسر اللعب بالشطرنج والنرد وغير ذلك من أنواع القمار. حتى إن لعب الصبيان بالجوز

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r5.claim: Fajtanibūhu means keep to one side of it; laʿallakum tufliḥūn means so that you may win the reward.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r5.anchor: { فاجتنبوه } أي كونوا على جانب منه أي في ناحية { لعلكم تفلحون } معناه لكي تفوزوا بالثواب

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r6.claim: First proof of prohibition: God calls these acts impurity, which is forbidden by consensus.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r6.anchor: أحدها: أنه سبحانه وصفها بالرجس وهو النجس والنجس محرم بلا خلاف

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r7.claim: Second proof of prohibition: God attributes these acts to Satan’s work.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r7.anchor: والثاني: أنه نسبها إلى عمل الشيطان وذلك يوجب تحريمها

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r8.claim: Third proof of prohibition: the command to avoid them requires abstention.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r8.anchor: والثالث: أنه أمر باجتنابها والأمر يقتضي الإيجاب

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r9.claim: Fourth proof of prohibition: God makes success depend on abstaining from these acts.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r9.anchor: والرابع: أنه جعل الفوز والفرح في اجتنابها

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r10.claim: The pronoun may refer to Satan’s work, so avoid every satanic practice listed, or to rijs, which covers wine and the other named acts.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r10.anchor: والهاء في قوله: { فاجتنبوه } راجعة إلى عمل الشيطان تقديره فاجتنبوا عمل الشيطان

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r11.claim: Wine is paired with idol worship to emphasize the severity of its prohibition.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r11.anchor: وقد قرن الله تعالى الخمر بعبادة الأوثان تغليظا في تحريمها

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r12.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r12.claim: Al-Baqir says a habitual drinker is like an idol worshipper.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r12.anchor: ولذلك قال الباقر: ع مدمن الخمر كعابد الوثن

TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r13.claim: The verse also prohibits every other dealing in wine, including selling, buying, and using it in any way.
TABRISI:5:90-91#2/r13.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على تحريم سائر التصرفات في الخمر من الشرب والبيع والشراء والاستعمال

THALABI:v4p106/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p106/r1.claim: Thaʿlabi says wine was explained earlier and now adduces warnings against drinking, making or keeping, and selling it.
THALABI:v4p106/r1.anchor: وقد مر تفسيره، فإن جمعه تحريمها وسنذكر أخبارا في الوعيد الوارد

THALABI:v4p106/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
THALABI:v4p106/r2.claim: The Prophet said God never combines wine and faith in one person.
THALABI:v4p106/r2.anchor: عن ابن المسيب عن عثمان بن عفان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله لا يجمع الخمر والإيمان

THALABI:v4p106/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p106/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p106/r3.claim: The Prophet compared a habitual wine drinker to a worshipper of idols.
THALABI:v4p106/r3.anchor: عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مدمن الخمر كعابد الوثن»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes wine to include every drink that ferments until it becomes strong and intoxicating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r1.anchor: وقد قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: "يريد الخمر من جميع الأشربة التي تخمر حتى تشتد وتسكر"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says wine comes from nine sources, including honey, grapes, raisins, dates, wheat, corn, barley, and sult.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r2.anchor: وقد قال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "الخمر من تسع: من البتع وهو العسل، ومن العنب، ومن الزبيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r3.claim: Maysir means gambling, which occurs in many forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r3.anchor: وقال في الميسر: "يريد القمار، وهو في أشياء كثيرة"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
