WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines maysir as gambling generally and traces its original form to gambling over a slaughtered camel.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r5.speaker: الأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني وأبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r5.claim: They differ on the camel's shares: al-Asma'i says twenty-eight, Abu Amr al-Shaybani ten, while Abu Ubayda does not know the number.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r5.anchor: في قول الأصمعي على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا، وفي قول أبي عمرو الشيباني على عشرة أجزاء، وقال أبو عبيدة: لا أعرف عدد الأجزاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r6.claim: Camel gambling is the paradigmatic form; all gambling is like maysir, and the detailed procedure is omitted here and treated in his book al-Maysir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r6.anchor: فهذا أجل الميسر، والقمار كله كالميسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r7.claim: He says the meanings, origins, and derivations of wine and maysir were discussed earlier in Surat al-Baqara.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p508#2/r7.anchor: قد ذكرنا في سورة البقرة معنى الخمر والميسر وأصلهما واشتقاقهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r1.claim: The anṣāb are the idols people erected and worshipped; naṣb is their singular.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أنصبتهم التي نصبوها يعبدونها، وواحدها نصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r2.claim: The azlām are arrows marked with the words good and evil; al-Farra and al-Zajjaj give the same interpretation for both terms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r2.anchor: وقال في الأزلام: إنها سهام مكتوب عليها خير وشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r3.claim: He directs readers to his earlier explanation of anṣāb and azlām at the verse about offerings on stone altars and divining arrows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r3.anchor: وقد ذكرنا معنى الأنصاب والأزلام في أول السورة عند قوله تعالى: {وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r4.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r4.claim: Some identify these azlām as the lots used in maysir; al-Azhari rejects this as a mistake.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن المراد بالأزلام ههنا: قداح الميسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r5.claim: In ordinary language rijs names anything detestable or a vile deed; the verb can mean that someone has done something ugly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r5.anchor: الرجس في اللغة: اسم لكل ما استقذر من عمل، يقال: رجس الرجل رجسا ورجس، إذا عمل عملا قبيحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r6.claim: The root's original sense is a loud, intense sound; a thunderous cloud illustrates it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r6.anchor: وأصل من الرجس بفتح الراء وهو شدة الصوت، يقال: سحاب رجاس، إذا كان شديد الصوت بالرعد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r7.claim: The term denotes a deed whose mention is intensely ugly and elevated in repulsiveness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r7.anchor: فكان الرجس العمل الذي يقبح ذكره جدا ويرتفع في القبح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r8.claim: An anonymous rājiz line cites rajjās as the word for thunderous sound.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r8.anchor: قال الراجز: وكل رجاس يسوق الرجسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God intensifies His condemnation by calling these things rijs and declares that Satan entices people toward them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p509/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): بالغ الله في ذم هذه الأشياء فسماها رجسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r1.claim: Ijtanibūhu means to keep to one side and away from it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فاجتنبوه}، أي: كونوا جانبا منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r2.claim: The pronoun in the command refers to rijs, which applies to wine and everything listed after it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r2.anchor: والهاء عائدة على الرجس (¬6)، والرجس واقع على الخمر وما ذكر بعدها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r3.claim: Wine is paired with idol worship to intensify the prohibition against drinking it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r3.anchor: وقد قرن الله تعالى تحريم الخمر بتحريم عبادة الأوثان تغليظا وإبلاغا في النهي عن شربها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r4.claim: The Prophet compares a habitual wine drinker to an idol worshipper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "مدمن الخمر كعابد الوثن"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r5.claim: The Prophet says that, after idol worship, the greatest thing his Lord forbade him was wine drinking and quarrelling with men, meaning hostility.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p510/r5.anchor: وقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "أكثر ما نهاني عنه ربي بعد عبادة الأوثان شرب الخمر وملاحاة الرجال"

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r1.claim: Al-maysir is gambling; yassartu means casting lots with arrows, and the person who does so is called yāsir, yāsirūn, yusr, or aysār.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r1.anchor: والميسر} القمار. يقال: يسرت: إذا ضربت بالقداح والضارب بها يقال له: ياسر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r2.claim: In harsh winter, wealthy and generous people slaughtered and divided a camel by arrows; the winner gave the shares to the needy, the benefit mentioned in 2:219.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r2.anchor: وكان أصحاب الثروة والأجواد في الشتاء عند شدة الزمان وكلبه ينحرون جزورا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r3.claim: People praised winning the arrow draw, disparaged those who declined it as abram, and called one such person a baram.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r3.anchor: وكانوا يتمادحون بأخذ القداح ويتسابون بتركها ويعيبون من لا ييسرون

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r4.claim: The anṣāb were stones worshiped in pre-Islamic times.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r4.anchor: والأنصاب} حجارة كانوا يعبدونها في الجاهلية.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r5.claim: Al-azlām are divining arrows, discussed earlier in this sūra.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r5.anchor: والأزلام} القداح. وقد ذكرتها في أول هذه السورة (5) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r6.claim: The root meaning of rijs is stench.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p145#3/r6.anchor:
والأزلام} القداح. وقد ذكرتها في أول هذه السورة (5) .
{رجس} وأصل الرجس: النتن.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r1.claim: Wine here means drinks fermented until they become strong and intoxicating.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r1.anchor: يعني: الأشربة التي تخمر حتى تشتد وتسكر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r2.claim: Maysir means every kind of gambling.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r4.claim: The azlām are lots or arrows used for divination, mentioned at the beginning of this sūra.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r4.anchor: والأزلام } قداح الاستقسام التي ذكرت في أول السورة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r5.claim: Rijs means something filthy and repugnant.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r5.anchor: رجس } قذر قبيح { من عمل الشيطان }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r6.claim: These things belong to Satan’s work, which he tempts human beings to do.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r6.anchor: من عمل الشيطان } مما يسوله الشيطان لبني آدم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:90-91/r7.claim: Avoid it by keeping away from it altogether.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r5.claim: After Sa'd drunkenly recited satire about an Anṣārī, was struck with a jawbone, and complained, the Prophet prayed for clarity and the final verses intensified wine's prohibition.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r5.anchor: Sa‘d, ensardan birinin hicvini mutazammın bir şiir okumuş, o da bir çene kemiğiyle vurup başını yarmış

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r6.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r6.claim: On hearing the final prohibition, Umar answered that they had completely desisted.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r6.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer bunu dinleyince “inteheynâ yâ Rabbi” yani “tamamen vazgeçtik yâ Rabbi!” demiştir.

ELMALILI:5:90/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the objects as drink, gambling, idols, and lots, calls them filthy work of Satan, and urges avoidance for deliverance.
ELMALILI:5:90/r1.anchor: İçki, kumar, putlar, kısmet çekilen zarlar hep şeytan işi murdar bir şeydir, onun için siz ondan kaçının ki yakayı kurtarasınız

ELMALILI:5:90/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r2.claim: Believers should avoid forbidden impurities, just as they had not prohibited wholesome lawful things.
ELMALILI:5:90/r2.anchor: Ey iman edenler helâl olan tayyibâtı tahrim etmediğiniz gibi haram olan habâisten de iyi sakınınız.

ELMALILI:5:90/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r3.claim: Hamr means intoxicating drinks, while meysir means lottery and gambling; Elmalılı directs readers to the earlier discussion in al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:5:90/r3.anchor: muhakkak hamr, yani müskirât ve meysir, yani piyango ve kumar

ELMALILI:5:90/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r4.claim: Anṣāb are stones erected for worship, along with other idols and graven images.
ELMALILI:5:90/r4.anchor: ensâb, yani ta‘abbüd için dikilmiş taş vesâir evsân ü asnâm

ELMALILI:5:90/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r5.claim: Azlām are gambling and lottery implements: sticks, arrows, and dice.
ELMALILI:5:90/r5.anchor: kumar ve piyango kalemleri, okları, zarları

ELMALILI:5:90/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r6.claim: Rijs is filth that sensible minds find repellent and disgusting.

ELMALILI:5:90/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r7.claim: Calling these things Satan’s work identifies them as the devil’s doing and incitement, warning that their evil is absolute or predominant.
ELMALILI:5:90/r7.anchor: şerr-i mahz veya gālib olduğuna tenbîhen مِّنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ buyurulmuş

ELMALILI:5:90/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r8.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith likening the wine drinker to an idol-worshipper, reinforcing the prohibition’s association with idolatry.
ELMALILI:5:90/r8.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi medlûlünce putperestlik kabîlinden gösterilmiş

ELMALILI:5:90/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r9.claim: The command is to shun the impure things themselves, and this abstention is made a means of hoping for success.
ELMALILI:5:90/r9.anchor: bizzat ‘aynlarından ictinab emredilmiş, sâdisen bu ictinab felâh ümidine bir sebep yapılmıştır.

ELMALILI:5:90/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r10.claim: This is the third and final revelation in the staged prohibition of intoxicants; the earlier stages were 4:43 and 2:219.
ELMALILI:5:90/r10.anchor: Bu âyet, müskirâtın men‘u tahrîmi hakkında üçüncü ve son olarak nâzil olan âyettir

ELMALILI:5:90/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:90/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:90/r11.claim: Elmalılı says the verse’s chief aim is to prohibit wine and gambling and establish their religious and worldly harms and burdens while clarifying Satan’s work.
ELMALILI:5:90/r11.anchor: asıl maksad hamr u meysirin tahrîmi olduğu ihtar ve bunların tahrîmini iktizâ eden dînî, dünyevî mefsedet ve veballerini takrir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r1.claim: Islam communicates obligations and trains people gradually, allowing time to absorb rules whose abrupt imposition could unsettle entrenched social practices.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r1.anchor: İslâm’da yükümlülüklerin tebliği ve insanın eğitimi konularında tedrîcîlik yani adım adım ilerleme yöntemi önemli bir yere sahiptir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r2.speaker: Hz. Âişe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r2.claim: Aisha said that if the Qur’an had initially prohibited drinking and adultery, people would have abandoned the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r2.anchor: Hz. Âişe şu sözleriyle bu hususu çok veciz bir biçimde ifade etmiştir: “Şayet Kur’an’ın ilk âyetleri ‘İçki içmeyin’

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r3.claim: Because drinking and gambling were widespread, revelation first prompted reflection and established faith and obedience; only then came a definitive ban, succeeding where America’s 1929 prohibition failed without that basis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r3.anchor: Buna karşılık, meselâ Amerika’da 1929 yılında devlet eliyle ve imkânlarıyla yürütülen içki yasağı girişimi, çok büyük maddî harcamalar yapılmasına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r4.claim: Tabari lists possible occasions: Umar’s plea for a categorical ruling, Sa‘d b. Abi Waqqas being injured after a drinking meal, or hostility after gambling losses; no cause is certain, but the command to desist is.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r4.anchor: Taberî bunları naklettikten sonra özetle şöyle der: Bu sebep, Hz. Ömer’in içki hakkında kesin bir buyruk gelmesi için Allah’a yalvarması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r6.claim: The text stresses social and religious damage, which is readily observed in ordinary experience, while scientific study can further establish the effects on body and mind.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r6.anchor: Âyette bunların daha çok sosyal hayatta açtığı yaralara ve dinî hayata vurduğu darbeye değinilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r8.claim: Even if drink has benefits and moderation is proposed, its greater harm and uncontrollability make a categorical, general prohibition the only effective remedy; Islam chose it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r8.anchor: zararı daha fazla olan, kontrolü de imkânsız bulunan bir nesneyi ve alışkanlığı ortadan kaldırmanın tek yolu kesin ve genel yasaklamadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r9.claim: The erected stones were set around the Kaaba by Arabs for sacrifices offered to idols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r9.anchor: “Dikili taşlar”dan maksat Araplar’ın, üzerinde putlar adına kurban kesmek için Kâbe’nin etrafına diktikleri taşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r10.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports an alternative reading in which the idols before which sacrifices were made, rather than the stones, are meant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r10.anchor: Bir yoruma göre burada, huzurunda kurban kesilen putların kendileri kastedilmiştir (İbn Atıyye, II, 232)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r11.claim: The divining arrows were used in pre-Islamic Arabia to predict whether an undertaking would end well; their use was linked to gambling and incompatible with monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r11.anchor: “Fal okları” da Câhiliye dönemi Arap geleneğinde önemli bir işe girişmeden önce bu işin sonunun iyi gelip gelmeyeceğini anlama amacıyla kullanılan oklardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r12.claim: Worship suggestive of serving other than God and reliance on baseless omens were condemned alongside drink and gambling as unbecoming of believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r12.anchor: Allah’tan başkasına kulluk anlayışını çağrıştıracak ve kişinin teşebbüs ruhunu birtakım temelsiz inanışlara kilitleyecek bu tür uygulamalar da içki ve kumar yasağının peşi sıra zikredilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r13.claim: Vows at shrines and sacrifices at religious figures’ graves risk drawing practitioners toward the condemned beliefs and unwittingly away from monotheism, even when intentions are good.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r13.anchor: yatırlar için adakta bulunma ve din ulularının mezarları yanında adak kurbanı kesilmesi uygulamalarının, bunları yapanları âyette ikaz edilen tehlikeli anlayışa yaklaştırdığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r14.claim: Modern superstition and lottery thinking persist despite scientific progress, showing the need for sound religious knowledge and revelation’s continuing guidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:90/r14.anchor: Modern toplumlarda kültür seviyesinin yükselmesine ve pozitif bilimler alanındaki büyük ilerlemelere rağmen, bâtıl inanışlara bel bağlamanın nicelik ve nitelik olarak küçümsenemeyecek boyutta olması

ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Al-Tayalisi transmits Ibn Umar's account of alcohol's three-stage prohibition: first 2:219 left people free to benefit, then 4:43 prohibited drinking near prayer, and finally 5:90 prompted the Prophet to declare it forbidden.
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: روى الطيالسي في مسنده عن ابن عمر قال نزل في الخمر ثلاث آيات فأول شيء

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the staged ban: 2:219 came first, drunken misrecitation prompted 4:43, then 5:90-91 ended drinking; a question about believers who died drinking prompted 5:93's reassurance.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r1.anchor: روى أحمد عن أبي هريرة قال قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وهم يشربون الخمر ويأكلون الميسر فسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنهما

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that two Anṣār tribes drank, became drunk, and attacked one another; after seeing their injuries, brothers blamed one another and resentment grew, prompting this verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p97/r2.anchor: وروى النسائي والبيهقي عن ابن عباس قال انما نزل تحريم الخمر في قبيلتين من قبائل الأنصار شربوا فلما أن ثمل القوم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r3.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas reports that before wine was prohibited he drank with a group of Muhajirun and Ansar, argued that the Muhajirun were better, and was struck on the nose with a jawbone; he told Muhammad, and the verse was revealed. Muslim transmits the report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r3.anchor: حدثني مصعب بن سعد بن أبي وقاص، عن أبيه قال: أتيت على نفر من المهاجرين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r4.claim: Umar repeatedly prayed for a clear ruling on wine: 2:219 came first, then 4:43 restricted prayer while drunk, and finally 5:90 came; when he heard “Will you then desist?” he answered that they had desisted.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p206/r4.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة، عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

BURHAN:v3p281/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p281/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p281/r1.claim: The reordered phrase means abstain from idols, which are a kind of impurity.
